Default is Aspect Fit, which never distorts; switch to Aspect Fill when you want it edge-to-edge and don't mind some cropping.

guides.name: Screen field: Fixed image width
guides.userNeed: Know what "Fixed image width" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Fixed image width
sections.description: Optionally pin the hero image to a set width with the slider (0–500) or by typing a number. Leave it empty in most cases — the image then sizes to the screen and stays responsive across devices, which almost always looks best on a landing page. Set a fixed width only when you need the image smaller than full-width or aligned to a specific size.

guides.name: Screen field: Fixed image height
guides.userNeed: Know what "Fixed image height" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Fixed image height
sections.description: Optionally pin the hero image to a set height with the slider (0–500) or by typing a number. Leave it empty to let the image keep its natural proportions from the width — best for most screens. Use a fixed height when you want a consistent banner size; to size by screen proportion instead, use 'Image height relative to container' below, which takes priority over this value.

guides.name: Screen field: Size the image by screen
guides.userNeed: Know what "Size the image by screen" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Size the image by screen
sections.description: Sizes the hero image as a percentage of the screen height (0 to 100%), so it scales with the device, the more responsive way to size a hero. If set, it overrides any fixed height above. A common starting point is 30 to 50% for a prominent banner that still leaves room for your title and button below; leave it empty to size by proportions instead.

guides.name: Screen field: How rounded the image is
guides.userNeed: Know what "How rounded the image is" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: How rounded the image is
sections.description: Rounds all four corners of the hero image; 0 is sharp and higher values (up to 50) make them softer and more rounded. The default is 0. A small radius around 8 to 16 gives a modern, friendly look; match it to the rounding used elsewhere in your funnel, like buttons and cards, so the page feels consistent.

guides.name: Screen field: Space around the image
guides.userNeed: Know what "Space around the image" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Space around the image
sections.description: Adds empty space on each side of the hero image (top, right, bottom, left) so it isn't flush against the screen edges or crammed next to the title. Leave it at the theme default in most cases. Increase a side when the image feels too tight against nearby content, or reduce it for a full-bleed, edge-to-edge look.

guides.name: Screen field: Where the image sits
guides.userNeed: Know what "Where the image sits" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Where the image sits
sections.description: On headline screens, this sets where the hero image sits relative to your title and subtitle — above the text, below it, or beside it. Lead with your strongest element: image-on-top when the visual is the hook, text-on-top when the headline does the selling. The preview updates instantly, so try a couple and keep whichever reads clearest.

guides.name: Screen field: Play Screen Animations
guides.userNeed: Know what "Play Screen Animations" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Play Screen Animations
sections.description: Turns on the entrance, exit, and element animations you set up in the screen's animation settings; when off, the screen simply appears instantly. Use it on intro and hero screens where motion feels polished and guides the eye. Leave it off on dense question screens where visitors want the controls ready to tap right away.

guides.name: Screen field: Reuse cached media
guides.userNeed: Know what "Reuse cached media" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Reuse cached media
sections.description: When on, the screen reuses media it has already cached instead of re-downloading it, which can speed up loading for visitors on slow or flaky connections. Leave it off by default for standard web ad funnels, since there's nothing to reuse until assets are cached. Turn it on only if you ship pre-bundled assets or expect a lot of poor-connectivity traffic.

guides.name: Screen field: Ask For A Device Permission
guides.userNeed: Know what "Ask For A Device Permission" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Ask For A Device Permission
sections.description: When on, this screen pops the phone's own permission request, notifications, location, or ad tracking, chosen in the field below, as it appears. This fires in the native app SDK, not on a plain web page. Put it on a screen that first explains why you need it so far more people tap Allow.

guides.name: Screen field: Which Permission To Ask For
guides.userNeed: Know what "Which Permission To Ask For" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Which Permission To Ask For
sections.description: Picks which device permission this screen requests: push notifications, ad tracking (needed for accurate ad attribution on iPhones), or location. Only shows when the permission request is turned on. Choose what your funnel truly needs, ad tracking if you rely on ad-network attribution, notifications for re-engaging users later.

guides.name: Screen field: Auto-Advance After A Delay
guides.userNeed: Know what "Auto-Advance After A Delay" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Auto-Advance After A Delay
sections.description: When on, the screen moves to the next step on its own after the countdown you set below, with a visible timer. Off by default. Great for splash or 'analyzing...' screens, but never use it where visitors must tap or answer, like questions or your paywall, or you'll skip them past the response or sale.

guides.name: Screen field: Auto-Advance Duration
guides.userNeed: Know what "Auto-Advance Duration" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Auto-Advance Duration
sections.description: The number of seconds or minutes (unit chosen below) before the screen moves on by itself, from 1 to 300. Only used when auto-advance is on. Keep it short, about 2 to 4 seconds for a splash or 'analyzing...' screen, so visitors aren't left waiting and bouncing.

guides.name: Screen field: Seconds Or Minutes
guides.userNeed: Know what "Seconds Or Minutes" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Seconds Or Minutes
sections.description: Sets whether the auto-advance duration above counts in seconds or minutes. Only shows when auto-advance is on. Seconds is the right choice for nearly every onboarding screen; minutes is rarely useful and risks visitors leaving before the screen ever advances.

guides.name: Screen field: Show an image or video
guides.userNeed: Know what "Show an image or video" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Show an image or video
sections.description: Turns the image or video block on or off for this screen; off means no visual is shown. Turn it on to add a supporting visual, since on a paid landing page a relevant image or video builds trust and lifts conversion. When enabled, it starts with sensible styling from your design theme that you can fine-tune in the fields below.

guides.name: Screen field: Image or video
guides.userNeed: Know what "Image or video" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Image or video
sections.description: Pick whether this screen shows an image or a video. Use an image for a fast, lightweight visual that loads instantly; use a video for short product demos or motion that holds attention (it can loop). Switching type clears the current media, so choose before you upload. Keep videos short and light so the page stays fast, since slow loads cost conversions on paid traffic.

guides.name: Screen field: The image for this screen
guides.userNeed: Know what "The image for this screen" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: The image for this screen
sections.description: Add this screen's image by uploading a file from your computer or pasting a direct image URL, then confirm it in the preview. Use a high-quality JPG or PNG that's on-message for the screen — uploads are optimized automatically for fast loading on every device. To replace it later, upload or paste a new source here.

guides.name: Screen field: The video for this screen
guides.userNeed: Know what "The video for this screen" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: The video for this screen
sections.description: Add a video by uploading a file or pasting a direct video URL. Keep it short (a few seconds, ideally under ~30s) and lightweight so the page loads fast — long or heavy videos hurt conversion on paid traffic. Uploads are converted automatically to play reliably across devices, and you can pair this with the loop option below to replay it continuously.

guides.name: Screen field: Where the media starts on top
guides.userNeed: Know what "Where the media starts on top" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Where the media starts on top
sections.description: Sets where the media begins from the top of the screen. Screen Top runs it edge-to-edge to the very top (great for a full-bleed hero), Navigation Bar starts it just below the header, and Safe Area keeps it clear of phone notches and rounded corners. Pick Screen Top for an immersive banner, Safe Area when nothing should ever be clipped. This is locked if you set a media height percentage below, which positions it for you.

guides.name: Screen field: How media fills its box
guides.userNeed: Know what "How media fills its box" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: How media fills its box
sections.description: Controls how the media fills its box. Aspect Fit shows the whole thing without cropping (you may see empty bars), Aspect Fill covers the box completely but may crop edges, and Scale to Fill stretches it, which distorts photos, so avoid that. The positional options (Top, Bottom, Center, and so on) crop to fill while keeping that part in view. Aspect Fill is the usual pick for an edge-to-edge banner; use Aspect Fit when nothing should be cropped.

guides.name: Screen field: How tall the media is
guides.userNeed: Know what "How tall the media is" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: How tall the media is
sections.description: Sets the media height as a share of the screen (0 to 100%), so it scales on every device; the default is 50%. Use a larger percentage for an immersive, image-led screen and a smaller one when you need room for the title, text, or button below; on a choice screen, keep it modest so the options stay visible without scrolling. Setting a value pins the media just below the header for a consistent layout.

guides.name: Screen field: How rounded the media is
guides.userNeed: Know what "How rounded the media is" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: How rounded the media is
sections.description: Rounds the corners of the media block; 0 is sharp and higher values (up to 50) make them softer. A small radius around 8 to 16 gives a modern, polished look; match it to the rounding on your buttons and cards so the whole screen feels consistent. Leave it at 0 for full-bleed media that touches the screen edges.

guides.name: Screen field: Replay the video on a loop
guides.userNeed: Know what "Replay the video on a loop" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Replay the video on a loop
sections.description: When on, the video replays continuously; when off, it plays once and stops on the last frame. Only applies to video media. Turn looping on for short ambient background clips that hold attention; turn it off for a demo or explainer you want watched once, so it doesn't loop distractingly while the visitor reads.

guides.name: Screen field: Space around the media
guides.userNeed: Know what "Space around the media" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Space around the media
sections.description: Adds empty space on the four sides of the media (top, right, bottom, left) so it isn't flush against the screen edges or neighboring content. Leave it at the default for a full-width visual. Increase a side to inset the media and give it a framed look with breathing room, rather than edge-to-edge.

guides.name: Screen field: Fade over the media
guides.userNeed: Know what "Fade over the media" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Fade over the media
sections.description: Lays a soft, see-through fade (usually dark) over the media so any text or button on top stays readable against a busy image. Turn it on whenever you place a title, subtitle, or button over the media; without it, light areas of the image can wash out your copy. When enabled, you get controls below to set the fade's height and color.

guides.name: Screen field: How far the fade extends
guides.userNeed: Know what "How far the fade extends" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: How far the fade extends
sections.description: Controls how far the fade reaches across the media (0 to 100%). Match it to where your text or button sits: if the copy is near the bottom, a 30 to 50% fade from that edge usually gives enough contrast without darkening the whole image. Increase it if text is still hard to read, decrease it to show more of the image clearly.

guides.name: Screen field: Color of the fade
guides.userNeed: Know what "Color of the fade" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Color of the fade
sections.description: Picks the color of the fade over the media. Use a dark color (usually black) behind light or white text, or a light color behind dark text; the fade goes from this color to fully transparent so the image still shows through. Match it to your background or brand color for a seamless look, and choose whichever direction gives your copy the strongest contrast.

guides.name: Screen field: How visitors choose
guides.userNeed: Know what "How visitors choose" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: How visitors choose
sections.description: Sets how people interact: browse only (no selection, like an intro list), pick one, or pick several. This also decides what's saved to the bound variable — pick-one stores a single value you can branch on, pick-several stores a set. Default to pick-one for most onboarding questions.

guides.name: Screen field: List or grid layout
guides.userNeed: Know what "List or grid layout" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: List or grid layout
sections.description: Choose whether choices stack in a single-column list or sit in a two-column grid. Use a list for text-heavy answers that need a full line each; use a grid when items have images or icons and you want a compact, visual picker. Switching to a grid unlocks the image, text, and checkbox layout controls. Default to a single-column list for plain answer choices.

guides.name: Screen field: What each choice shows
guides.userNeed: Know what "What each choice shows" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: What each choice shows
sections.description: Pick which parts each choice displays — title only, image plus title, checkbox with title and subtitle, and so on; available combos depend on your selection mode and layout. Adding an element reveals its style controls and means you must supply that content (image or subtitle) on every item. Default to title (plus a checkbox for multi-select) and add an image only when it aids the choice.

guides.name: Screen field: Shuffle item order
guides.userNeed: Know what "Shuffle item order" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Shuffle item order
sections.description: When enabled, randomizes the order items appear to users on each view. Useful for A/B testing, survey randomization, and reducing position bias in multi-select scenarios.

guides.name: Screen field: Cap on multi-select picks
guides.userNeed: Know what "Cap on multi-select picks" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Cap on multi-select picks
sections.description: Limits how many items a visitor can choose on a multi-select screen. Set a small cap (e.g. 3) to keep answers focused and the next step manageable; leave it unlimited to let them pick freely. This control only appears on multi-select screens and is ignored everywhere else.

guides.name: Screen field: Vertical alignment of items
guides.userNeed: Know what "Vertical alignment of items" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Vertical alignment of items
sections.description: Aligns each choice's content to the top, center, or bottom of its cell. It's most noticeable in grid layouts where cells are taller than their content; center usually looks balanced. In simple lists it has little visible effect, so center is a safe default.

guides.name: Screen field: Even grid cell heights
guides.userNeed: Know what "Even grid cell heights" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Even grid cell heights
sections.description: On a grid, choose whether all cells stretch to the same maximum height for tidy, even rows, or each cell sizes to its own content (giving rows of varying height). Turn it on for a clean, consistent grid; turn it off when items have very different content lengths. Only applies to grid layouts.

guides.name: Screen field: Unselected item look
guides.userNeed: Know what "Unselected item look" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Unselected item look
sections.description: The default look of each choice before it's tapped — background, border, corner radius, and an optional gradient. Keep it neutral and calm so the selected state can stand out; the contrast between this and the selected look is what tells visitors their tap registered. Pair it with the Selected item look.

guides.name: Screen field: Selected item look
guides.userNeed: Know what "Selected item look" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Selected item look
sections.description: How a choice looks once tapped — background, border, corner radius, and optional gradient. Make it clearly distinct from the unselected look (an accent border or filled background) so visitors get instant confirmation; weak feedback here causes hesitation and drop-off. Your theme's accent color is a reliable choice.

guides.name: Screen field: Padding inside each item
guides.userNeed: Know what "Padding inside each item" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Padding inside each item
sections.description: The space between each item's edge and its content (title, image, checkbox), set per side — top, end, bottom, start. More padding makes items feel roomy and easier to tap; too little looks cramped. Around 12–16px on all sides reads well on mobile, and the setting applies to every item.

guides.name: Screen field: Margin around the whole list
guides.userNeed: Know what "Margin around the whole list" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Margin around the whole list
sections.description: The outer space between the screen edges and the first and last items, set per side (top, end, bottom, start). Use it to keep the list off the screen edges and aligned with your other sections. This is the outside spacing — for the gap inside each item use Padding inside each item instead.

guides.name: Screen field: Gap between choices
guides.userNeed: Know what "Gap between choices" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Gap between choices
sections.description: The spacing between adjacent choices — a vertical gap in lists, the gap between cells in grids. Around 8–12px keeps items clearly separate and easy to tap without wasting space. Increase it for a more airy feel, or decrease it to fit more options above the fold.

guides.name: Screen field: Grid cell proportions
guides.userNeed: Know what "Grid cell proportions" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Grid cell proportions
sections.description: Sets each grid cell's height as a percentage of its width: 100 is square, above 100 makes taller cells, below 100 makes wider, shorter cells. Pick taller cells for image-led options and square for balanced icon-and-text choices. Only appears on two-column grids — try 100 first, then adjust to fit your content.

guides.name: Screen field: Image area in each card
guides.userNeed: Know what "Image area in each card" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Image area in each card
sections.description: On grid cards that show an image, this sets the image region as a whole: where it sits in the card, how tall it is (a fixed height or sized to fit its content), and the spacing around it. By default it fits the content, but setting one fixed height keeps every card's image lined up at the same level, which looks more polished and trustworthy on an ad landing page. This shapes the image's container only; the image's own size and corners are set separately in the item image styles.

guides.name: Screen field: Text area in each card
guides.userNeed: Know what "Text area in each card" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Text area in each card
sections.description: On grid cards with an image, this sets the title-and-subtitle region as a block: where it sits in the card, how tall it is (a fixed height or sized to fit its content), and the spacing around it. It fits the content by default, but choosing one fixed height keeps the text blocks aligned across every card so the row reads as a clean, scannable set. This controls the text region's position only; the actual fonts and colors of the title and subtitle are set in their own style sections.

guides.name: Screen field: Checkbox placement in grid cells
guides.userNeed: Know what "Checkbox placement in grid cells" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Checkbox placement in grid cells
sections.description: On grid cells, show or hide the selection checkbox and place it in a corner (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, or bottom-right) with an optional offset. Keep it visible on multi-select grids so visitors can see what they've picked; top-right is a common, unobtrusive spot. Only appears on grid layouts.

guides.name: Screen field: Item title text style
guides.userNeed: Know what "Item title text style" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Item title text style
sections.description: Typography for every item's title — size, weight, color, alignment, line height, plus an optional background chip (color, opacity, radius) and padding. It's a shared template, so an edit restyles all items at once. Leave it on theme defaults for consistency, adjusting size or color only to improve readability against the item background.

guides.name: Screen field: Item subtitle text style
guides.userNeed: Know what "Item subtitle text style" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Item subtitle text style
sections.description: Typography for the item subtitle — size, weight, color, alignment, line height, optional background, and padding, applied to all items as a shared template. Keep the subtitle visually quieter than the title (smaller, muted color) so it reads as supporting text. Only appears when your item layout includes a subtitle.

guides.name: Screen field: Item image look
guides.userNeed: Know what "Item image look" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Item image look
sections.description: Size and look of each item's image — width, height, corner radius, padding, and how it fits its box (fit shows the whole image with possible empty space; fill crops to cover the box). Keep a consistent size and small radius so cards look uniform; choose fill for photos and fit for logos or icons you don't want cropped. Only appears when the layout includes an image.

guides.name: Screen field: Checkbox look
guides.userNeed: Know what "Checkbox look" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Checkbox look
sections.description: Appearance of the selection checkbox — shape (square or circle), checked color, unchecked color, and padding. Use your theme's accent for the checked color so a tap reads clearly as selected, matching the selected-item look. Circle suits pick-one (radio style), square suits multi-select. Only appears when the layout includes a checkbox or on grids.

guides.name: Screen field: Choose where the answer is saved
guides.userNeed: Know what "Choose where the answer is saved" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Choose where the answer is saved
sections.description: Pick which variable stores this screen's answer, or create a new one on the spot. Reuse an existing variable when this screen asks about the same thing as another screen (so all answers feed one value), and create a new one for a brand-new question. This is the key step: nothing downstream (branching, analytics, paywall personalization) works until a variable is chosen here.

guides.name: Screen field: Name the new variable
guides.userNeed: Know what "Name the new variable" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Name the new variable
sections.description: A readable name for the variable you're creating, like User Goal, that must be unique across the funnel. It becomes the reference you use elsewhere — usually a lowercased, underscored form such as @user_goal in dynamic text and conditions. Pick a clear name that describes the answer (User Goal, Experience Level) rather than the screen, since later references depend on it and you won't want to rename it.

guides.name: Screen field: What kind of value it stores
guides.userNeed: Know what "What kind of value it stores" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: What kind of value it stores
sections.description: Sets the kind of value this variable holds, which must fit the screen. Use Choice for single-select screens, Multiple choices for multi-select lists or grids where visitors pick several, Number for numeric input like age or weight, and Text for free-form typed answers. The screen only offers compatible types, and the Choice options you can branch and report on are defined below.

guides.name: Screen field: Internal note (optional)
guides.userNeed: Know what "Internal note (optional)" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Internal note (optional)
sections.description: An optional internal note explaining what this variable is for. It only shows as a tooltip in the editor when you hover the variable later — visitors never see it and it has no effect on the funnel. A one-line note like "visitor's primary fitness goal" is worth adding so you and teammates remember the variable's purpose when reusing it across screens.

guides.name: Screen field: List the stored answers
guides.userNeed: Know what "List the stored answers" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: List the stored answers
sections.description: For Choice and Multiple-choice variables, list the values this variable can store, such as lose_weight, build_muscle, or stay_fit; add, rename, or remove them here. These stored values are separate from the labels visitors see — you connect each one to a visible item in the Value Mapping table below. Keep one option per real answer so your routing and analytics stay clean.

guides.name: Screen field: The stored value for this option
guides.userNeed: Know what "The stored value for this option" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: The stored value for this option
sections.description: This is the value saved to the variable and used in conditions and analytics, not the text visitors see (that lives on the list or grid item). Keep it stable and lowercase with underscores, like lose_weight. You can rename it, but that changes every place it's referenced, so avoid renaming after the funnel is published and collecting data.

guides.name: Screen field: Link a choice to this value
guides.userNeed: Know what "Link a choice to this value" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Link a choice to this value
sections.description: Connect this option to the on-screen choice (the list or grid row) that should set it, so when a visitor picks that row the variable stores this value. Each visible choice should map to one option so answers record correctly, and several options can point to the same row if needed. If a choice has no option mapped to it, the editor flags it as unmapped, so fix that before publishing or it won't record an answer.

guides.name: Screen field: Add an option value
guides.userNeed: Know what "Add an option value" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Add an option value
sections.description: Type a value for a new option on this variable and click Add; it joins the options list and the mapping table below. Use a stable, lowercase, underscore-style value such as maintain_weight so routing and analytics stay clean. After adding it, map it to the matching on-screen item below — otherwise a visitor choosing that answer won't store anything.

guides.name: Screen field: Add points based on answers
guides.userNeed: Know what "Add points based on answers" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Add points based on answers
sections.description: Optional and advanced: have each answer on this screen add points to a number variable, like a quiz or lead-qualification score. You can later branch on the total (high score to a premium paywall) or send it to analytics. Skip this unless you're scoring answers, since most screens don't need it.

guides.name: Screen field: Which score this adds to
guides.userNeed: Know what "Which score this adds to" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Which score this adds to
sections.description: Choose the number variable this answer adds points to, such as a quiz_score or lead_score total. Only Number-type variables appear here, so if the list is empty, create a number variable first. Use one shared score variable across all the screens you want to total up, with the points set in the score value field.

guides.name: Screen field: Points this answer adds
guides.userNeed: Know what "Points this answer adds" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Points this answer adds
sections.description: The whole number this answer adds to the running total in the target score variable when a visitor selects this option. Give higher-intent answers larger values and weaker ones smaller or zero, for example 'ready to buy' = 10 and 'just browsing' = 1. Keep a consistent scale across all answers so the final total is meaningful for branching or analytics.

guides.name: Screen field: Rebuild options from the items
guides.userNeed: Know what "Rebuild options from the items" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Rebuild options from the items
sections.description: A shortcut that rebuilds this variable's options from the screen's current list or grid items so the stored values match what's on screen, handy after you've added or changed items and don't want to re-enter each option by hand. Warning: it replaces the existing options (a confirmation shows old versus new first), so custom options or mappings not present in the items can be lost. Avoid it when the variable is shared with other screens, and most funnels rarely need it once options are set.

guides.name: Screen field: What the field accepts
guides.userNeed: Know what "What the field accepts" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: What the field accepts
sections.description: Tells the field what kind of value to accept — plain text, a whole number, a decimal, a date, or an email — and automatically applies basic checks plus the right phone keyboard. Use Email for email capture and plain text for open answers. Picking the correct type blocks bad data, keeping any branching, analytics, or CRM that reads this answer reliable.

guides.name: Screen field: Color of typed answers
guides.userNeed: Know what "Color of typed answers" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Color of typed answers
sections.description: Sets the color of the text a visitor types into this field; the gray placeholder hint has its own separate color. Pick a color with strong contrast against the field background (use a light color on dark themes) so answers stay legible. Easy-to-read fields are easier to fill in, which protects completion on your data-collection screens.

guides.name: Screen field: Fill behind the input
guides.userNeed: Know what "Fill behind the input" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Fill behind the input
sections.description: Sets the fill color inside the input box. Most funnels leave it clear so the screen background shows through, or use a subtle light fill to make the tappable field stand out. Just make sure it contrasts with the typed-text color so answers stay easy to read and people don't abandon the question.

guides.name: Screen field: Color of the field outline
guides.userNeed: Know what "Color of the field outline" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Color of the field outline
sections.description: Sets the color of the field's outline, which only appears when the Border Style is an underline or a full box. Use a tone from your theme — an accent or a soft neutral — so the field's edges read clearly as something to tap and type into. A visible outline helps people recognize and fill in the field.

guides.name: Screen field: Thickness of the outline
guides.userNeed: Know what "Thickness of the outline" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Thickness of the outline
sections.description: Controls how thick the field's outline is, from 0 to 50 pixels (default 1). Keep it at 1-2 pixels for a clean, modern look and only go thicker for a deliberately bold style. A visible but restrained outline helps people spot the field at a glance and answer faster.

guides.name: Screen field: Pick the field outline style
guides.userNeed: Know what "Pick the field outline style" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Pick the field outline style
sections.description: Chooses how the field is outlined: a bottom underline under the text, a bottom underline with room for an icon, or a full box around the whole field. A full box reads most clearly as a place to type, while underline styles feel lighter. Your pick here also decides whether the Border Color and Border Width settings actually show.

guides.name: Screen field: Font for the field
guides.userNeed: Know what "Font for the field" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Font for the field
sections.description: Picks the font used for both the placeholder hint and what the visitor types. Leave it on the system font unless you have a brand font, and match whatever the rest of your funnel uses. Consistent type keeps the page feeling polished and trustworthy, which matters when you're paying for the traffic.

guides.name: Screen field: Size of the field text
guides.userNeed: Know what "Size of the field text" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Size of the field text
sections.description: Sets how large the text in the field appears, from 0 to 50 points (default 15). Keep it around 15-17 points so answers are comfortable to read on a phone. Text that's too small is hard to read on mobile, where most ad traffic lands, and can quietly drag down completion.

guides.name: Screen field: Weight of the field text
guides.userNeed: Know what "Weight of the field text" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Weight of the field text
sections.description: Sets how heavy the field text looks, from light (300) to bold (700), with regular (400) as the default. Regular is right for almost every input field. Keeping it regular makes the text read like an editable answer rather than a heading, so the field stays obvious and easy to use.

guides.name: Screen field: Line spacing in the field
guides.userNeed: Know what "Line spacing in the field" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Line spacing in the field
sections.description: Sets the vertical gap between lines of typed text (0-50pt, default 18). It only shows when an answer wraps onto multiple lines, so for normal single-line questions leave it at the default. Adjust it only if you've allowed long, multi-line responses and they feel too cramped or too loose.

guides.name: Screen field: How the text lines up
guides.userNeed: Know what "How the text lines up" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: How the text lines up
sections.description: Lines up the placeholder and typed text to the left, center, or right (default center). Left is the most familiar for input fields and the easiest to scan, while center suits short, decorative prompts. Pick whichever keeps the answer clearly readable for what you're collecting.

guides.name: Screen field: Override mobile keyboard input type
guides.userNeed: Know what "Override mobile keyboard input type" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Override mobile keyboard input type
sections.description: Forces a specific keyboard on mobile devices (Email, Numeric, Decimal, Phone, URL, etc.). Leave as Auto (from field type) to let the system derive keyboard type from Field Type setting.

guides.name: Screen field: Focus field when screen loads
guides.userNeed: Know what "Focus field when screen loads" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Focus field when screen loads
sections.description: When enabled, the field automatically receives focus and opens the keyboard when the screen appears. Default is true. Useful for primary input fields.

guides.name: Screen field: Space inside the field
guides.userNeed: Know what "Space inside the field" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Space inside the field
sections.description: Sets the breathing room between the text or icon and the field's edges, on the top, right, bottom, and left. Generous spacing makes the field a bigger, easier tap target and keeps text from crowding the outline. If the field feels cramped on a phone, increase the top and bottom spacing.

guides.name: Screen field: Space around the field
guides.userNeed: Know what "Space around the field" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Space around the field
sections.description: Sets the gap OUTSIDE the field, separating it from the title above and anything below, on the top, right, bottom, and left. Use it to give the field room to breathe within the screen. This is the space around the field — distinct from Internal Padding, which is the space inside it.

guides.name: Screen field: Set placeholder hint text
guides.userNeed: Know what "Set placeholder hint text" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Set placeholder hint text
sections.description: Hint text displayed in the field when empty, guiding users on what to enter. Can be localized per locale. Styling controlled by text appearance settings.

guides.name: Screen field: Color of the hint text
guides.userNeed: Know what "Color of the hint text" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Color of the hint text
sections.description: Sets the color of the faint hint shown while the field is empty, separate from the color of what the visitor types (default is a light gray, #999999). Keep it dimmer than the typed-text color so people can tell the hint from a real answer, but not so faint it disappears against your background.

guides.name: Screen field: Custom format rule (advanced)
guides.userNeed: Know what "Custom format rule (advanced)" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Custom format rule (advanced)
sections.description: An optional advanced rule that forces the typed value to match an exact pattern before the visitor can continue. Most funnels leave this empty and rely on Field Type instead — for emails the Email type already checks the format. Use it only for special shapes like postal or phone codes; if input fails, the Error Message you set is shown.

guides.name: Screen field: Set validation error message
guides.userNeed: Know what "Set validation error message" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Set validation error message
sections.description: Message displayed when user input fails validation (does not match Validation Regex or Field Type). Shown to guide correction. Can be localized per locale.

guides.name: Screen field: Fill behind the error text
guides.userNeed: Know what "Fill behind the error text" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Fill behind the error text
sections.description: Sets a fill color behind the validation error message that appears when an answer is rejected. Usually leave it transparent so only the red text shows; add a subtle tint only if you want the error to read like a banner. Whatever you choose, keep enough contrast with the error text so the message stays readable and users can quickly fix and continue.

guides.name: Screen field: Color of the error message
guides.userNeed: Know what "Color of the error message" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Color of the error message
sections.description: Sets the color of the error text shown when an answer fails validation (default red, #FF3B30). Keep it red or another high-contrast warning color so people instantly see that their input was rejected and needs fixing. A clear error keeps them from giving up before they can continue.

guides.name: Screen field: Font of the error text
guides.userNeed: Know what "Font of the error text" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Font of the error text
sections.description: Sets the typeface for the validation error message shown when an answer is rejected. Leave it on your theme/system font unless you have a specific brand font, and match it to the field's font so the error looks like part of the same form. A consistent error style keeps the screen feeling polished and helps users trust and fix the field fast.

guides.name: Screen field: Size of the error text
guides.userNeed: Know what "Size of the error text" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Size of the error text
sections.description: Sets the point size of the validation error message. Keep it a touch smaller than the field text (about 12-13pt) so it reads as a secondary note, but not so small it's hard to read on a phone. A legible error helps users spot and fix a rejected answer instead of abandoning the screen.

guides.name: Screen field: Boldness of the error text
guides.userNeed: Know what "Boldness of the error text" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Boldness of the error text
sections.description: Sets how heavy the error message looks (for example 400 regular or 600 semibold). Regular (400) works in most cases; step up to 600 if you want the error to stand out more. Paired with the red color, a bit more weight helps users notice and correct a rejected answer so they keep moving through the funnel.

guides.name: Screen field: Where the error text sits
guides.userNeed: Know what "Where the error text sits" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Where the error text sits
sections.description: Aligns the validation error message to the left, center, or right. Match it to the field's own text alignment (left is typical) so the message sits naturally under the input. Keeping them aligned makes it obvious which field was rejected, so users fix it quickly and don't stall.

guides.name: Screen field: Optional icon in the field
guides.userNeed: Know what "Optional icon in the field" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Optional icon in the field
sections.description: Adds a small image — like a mail or person glyph — to the left of the input to hint at what the field is for. It's optional, and you can upload a different image for each language. It only appears with a Border Style that leaves room for an icon, and its size and rounding come from the icon's image style settings.

guides.name: Screen field: Width of the field icon
guides.userNeed: Know what "Width of the field icon" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Width of the field icon
sections.description: Sets how wide the icon beside the input is (0-500px). Keep it small, around 20-24px, so it fits neatly next to the text, and usually match it to the icon height for a clean square glyph. Oversized icons crowd the field and make the input look heavier than it needs to.

guides.name: Screen field: Height of the field icon
guides.userNeed: Know what "Height of the field icon" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Height of the field icon
sections.description: Sets how tall the icon beside the input is (0-500px). Keep it around 20-24px so it lines up with the text, and usually match it to the icon width so the glyph stays square and undistorted. A right-sized icon reads as a helpful cue rather than visual clutter.

guides.name: Screen field: How the icon fills its space
guides.userNeed: Know what "How the icon fills its space" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: How the icon fills its space
sections.description: Controls how the icon sits inside its box: Fit keeps the whole image visible and may leave a little padding, Fill keeps proportions but crops the edges, and Stretch fills the box and can distort the image. Use Fit for logos and glyphs — it's the safe default — unless you specifically want a cropped or stretched look.

guides.name: Screen field: Rounding the icon corners
guides.userNeed: Know what "Rounding the icon corners" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Rounding the icon corners
sections.description: Rounds the corners of the icon image (0-50px, default 0 for square). Leave it at 0 for normal line or glyph icons; raise it only for a photo or avatar-style icon you want to soften or make circular. It has little visible effect on transparent line icons, so most fields can skip it.

guides.name: Screen field: Gap between icon and text
guides.userNeed: Know what "Gap between icon and text" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Gap between icon and text
sections.description: Sets the horizontal space between the field's icon and the text the visitor types (default 8 pixels). The default works for most fields — nudge it up a little if the icon and text feel cramped, or down for a tighter look. The goal is an icon and placeholder that sit comfortably balanced.

guides.name: Screen field: Slide content template
guides.userNeed: Know what "Slide content template" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Slide content template
sections.description: Sets which layers each slide shows: Image Only is just the picture, Image + Title adds one headline, Image + Title + Subtitle adds a supporting line, and Image + Title + 2 Subtitles shows all four text layers. Choosing a richer template reveals its matching text and style fields below. Default to Image + Title for clean, fast-reading slides and add subtitles only when each slide genuinely needs more copy.

guides.name: Screen field: Total play time
guides.userNeed: Know what "Total play time" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Total play time
sections.description: The total time in seconds for the whole carousel to play through once before it stops or the visitor moves on (0.1–120s). This total is split across slides by each slide's timing slider, so changing it speeds up or slows every slide proportionally. Start around 3–5 seconds per slide (about 12–20s for four slides) — long enough to read each line, short enough to keep momentum and avoid stalling the visitor.

guides.name: Screen field: Slide headline
guides.userNeed: Know what "Slide headline" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Slide headline
sections.description: The main headline on this slide, shown only when the slide template includes a title. Keep it short and benefit-led so it lands in the few seconds the slide is on screen. You can drop in the visitor's earlier answers with @variable, plus countdown timers and styled label chips; if your funnel runs in several languages, you edit this text per language.

guides.name: Screen field: Slide supporting line
guides.userNeed: Know what "Slide supporting line" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Slide supporting line
sections.description: The line under the headline, shown only when the slide template is Image + Title + Subtitle or richer. Use it to back up the headline with a quick proof point or detail rather than repeat it. It supports @variable personalization, countdown timers, and styled chips, is edited per language, and only appears after you set a slide template that includes a subtitle.

guides.name: Screen field: Slide extra line
guides.userNeed: Know what "Slide extra line" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Slide extra line
sections.description: A third text line below the supporting line, available only with the Image + Title + 2 Subtitles template. Use it sparingly for one last small detail like a disclaimer or extra proof, since four text layers over an image quickly overcrowd a slide and slow reading. Supports @variable personalization, countdown timers, and styled chips, and is edited per language.

guides.name: Screen field: Slide picture
guides.userNeed: Know what "Slide picture" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Slide picture
sections.description: The image shown on this slide, required on every slide no matter which template you pick. Drag-and-drop or click to upload, and Segmently serves a fast-loading optimized version automatically. Use a high-quality picture that matches the slide's message; how it fills the slide is set in Image styles below, and a slide left without an image shows blank, so set one on every slide before publishing.

guides.name: Screen field: How long this slide shows
guides.userNeed: Know what "How long this slide shows" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: How long this slide shows
sections.description: A two-thumb slider that sets the window, as a share of the carousel's total duration, during which this slide is on screen. Drag the thumbs apart to give this slide a longer share, which leaves less time for the others. For example, a 25% window at a 20-second total keeps this slide visible about 5 seconds; keep slides spread evenly and only widen the most persuasive one.

guides.name: Screen field: Title look and spacing
guides.userNeed: Know what "Title look and spacing" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Title look and spacing
sections.description: Open this to override how the carousel's headline looks: font size, weight, color, alignment, and the padding around the text. It only shows when the template includes a title. Leave it untouched to inherit your theme so screens stay consistent; change it only when one carousel needs a bigger or bolder headline, and note the overrides apply to the title on every slide.

guides.name: Screen field: Supporting line look
guides.userNeed: Know what "Supporting line look" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Supporting line look
sections.description: Open this to override the supporting line's font size, weight, color, alignment, and the padding around it; it shows only when the template includes a subtitle. Keep this line visually lighter than the headline (smaller or thinner) so the slide reads in the right order. Leave it on theme defaults for consistency unless this carousel needs a custom look, and remember changes apply to every slide.

guides.name: Screen field: Extra line look
guides.userNeed: Know what "Extra line look" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Extra line look
sections.description: Open this to override the third line's font size, weight, color, alignment, and the padding around it; it appears only with the Image + Title + 2 Subtitles template. Style it as the smallest, quietest text so it never competes with the headline or supporting line. Leave it on theme defaults unless you truly need a change, since overrides apply to this line on every slide of the carousel.

guides.name: Screen field: Image size and fit
guides.userNeed: Know what "Image size and fit" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Image size and fit
sections.description: Open this to control the slide image's width, height, corner radius, and how it fills its box: Fit shows the whole image (may leave bands), Fill covers the box (edges may crop), Crop trims to the exact box, and Tile repeats it. You also set the padding around the image. Fill is the usual choice for full-bleed slides and Fit keeps the whole graphic visible; settings apply to the image on every slide.

guides.name: Screen field: Image box height and position
guides.userNeed: Know what "Image box height and position" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Image box height and position
sections.description: Controls the box that holds each slide's image, separate from the image's own styling. Set how tall the box is (Auto fits the image, Fixed is an exact pixel height, Percent is a share of the slide), where the image sits inside it, and the padding around it. Leave it on Auto unless you want every slide's image to occupy the same vertical space so slides don't jump in size as visitors swipe.

guides.name: Screen field: Text box height and position
guides.userNeed: Know what "Text box height and position" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Text box height and position
sections.description: Controls the box that holds all of a slide's text (title, subtitle, detail) as a group, separate from styling each line. Set how tall the box is (Auto fits the text, Fixed is exact pixels, Percent is a share of the slide), where the text block sits, and the padding around it. Leave it on Auto unless you want text anchored the same way on every slide, for example always sitting in the lower third over the image.

guides.name: Screen field: Select progress stepper layout
guides.userNeed: Know what "Select progress stepper layout" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Select progress stepper layout
sections.description: Determines the visual layout for progress steps. Circle displays steps as an orbital arrangement (no image container); Image Container First and Chart Container First show image/text in a container with progress bar. Defines which content elements are shown in each segment (image visibility, title, subtitle, description).

guides.name: Screen field: How long the progress runs
guides.userNeed: Know what "How long the progress runs" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: How long the progress runs
sections.description: Total time, in seconds (1-120), for the progress sequence to advance through all its steps before the screen continues. Aim for about 4-8 seconds: long enough to feel like real work is happening for the user, short enough to avoid drop-off. Use the play/pause preview to test the pacing against your step text.

guides.name: Screen field: Color of the empty track
guides.userNeed: Know what "Color of the empty track" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Color of the empty track
sections.description: Color of the unfilled part of the progress bar — the portion not yet completed. Defaults to light gray (#E0E0E0), which works for most screens. Keep it clearly lighter than the fill color so the user can read their progress at a glance, or match your page background for a subtler look.

guides.name: Screen field: Color of the completed portion
guides.userNeed: Know what "Color of the completed portion" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Color of the completed portion
sections.description: Color of the filled part of the progress bar that grows as the sequence advances, signaling completion to the user. Defaults to green (#4CAF50). Use your brand accent or a clearly positive color, and keep strong contrast against the empty track so progress reads instantly.

guides.name: Screen field: How thick the progress bar is
guides.userNeed: Know what "How thick the progress bar is" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: How thick the progress bar is
sections.description: Height of the filled bar in pixels (0-50, default 4px). 4-8px reads as a clean, modern bar; go thicker only for a bold, attention-grabbing indicator. Set it equal to or greater than the track thickness so the fill sits flush over the track instead of looking sunken.

guides.name: Screen field: How thick the empty track is
guides.userNeed: Know what "How thick the empty track is" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: How thick the empty track is
sections.description: Height of the background track in pixels (0-50, default 4px). Keep it equal to the fill thickness for a standard flat bar — the safe choice for most screens. Make it larger than the fill only if you want a recessed groove look, since mismatched values change how the fill sits inside the track.

guides.name: Screen field: Space around the progress bar
guides.userNeed: Know what "Space around the progress bar" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Space around the progress bar
sections.description: Sets the empty space, in pixels, on each side of the progress bar: top, right, bottom, left. The default is usually 0 for a tight bar that sits close to your content; add top and bottom padding to give it room from the title or image above and below. On an ad funnel a progress bar with a little breathing room reads as a quick, low-effort flow, which keeps people moving forward.

guides.name: Screen field: Split between media and progress
guides.userNeed: Know what "Split between media and progress" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Split between media and progress
sections.description: Percentage of the screen's vertical space (0-100, default 50%) given to the image/text area; the rest goes to the progress area. Raise it above 50% when your image or step text needs more room, or lower it to make the progress bar more prominent. This appears only for the Image First or Chart First layouts and is hidden for the orbital Circle layout.

guides.name: Screen field: Configure segment title text
guides.userNeed: Know what "Configure segment title text" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Configure segment title text
sections.description: Text styling for segment titles including font size, weight, family, color, line height, and letter spacing. Title text is editable per segment with template variable support (@variable, @link, @countdown).

guides.name: Screen field: Space around the title
guides.userNeed: Know what "Space around the title" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Space around the title
sections.description: Sets the empty space, in pixels, on each side of the step title: top, right, bottom, left. The default is usually 0; add bottom padding to separate the title from the subtitle below, or side padding to keep long titles off the screen edges. A clear, uncrowded title is the first thing visitors read, so the small spacing tweak helps them grasp the offer fast and stay in the funnel.

guides.name: Screen field: Configure segment subtitle text
guides.userNeed: Know what "Configure segment subtitle text" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Configure segment subtitle text
sections.description: Text styling for segment subtitles including font size, weight, family, color, line height, and letter spacing. Subtitle text is editable per segment with template variable support.

guides.name: Screen field: Space around the subtitle
guides.userNeed: Know what "Space around the subtitle" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Space around the subtitle
sections.description: Sets the empty space, in pixels, on each side of the step subtitle: top, right, bottom, left. The default is usually 0; add top padding to set the subtitle off from the title above and bottom padding to separate it from the description below. Adjust it only when the subtitle feels cramped against neighboring text, so the supporting line stays easy to scan and reinforces your pitch.

guides.name: Screen field: Configure segment description text
guides.userNeed: Know what "Configure segment description text" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Configure segment description text
sections.description: Text styling for segment descriptions including font size, weight, family, color, line height, and letter spacing. Description text is editable per segment with template variable support.

guides.name: Screen field: Space around the description
guides.userNeed: Know what "Space around the description" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Space around the description
sections.description: Sets the empty space, in pixels, on each side of the step description: top, right, bottom, left. The default is usually 0; add top padding to separate the description from the subtitle above, or side padding to keep multi-line text off the screen edges. Comfortable spacing makes longer copy easy to read, which keeps visitors absorbing your value and tapping through.

guides.name: Screen field: Style the step image
guides.userNeed: Know what "Style the step image" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Style the step image
sections.description: Controls how each step's image looks: how it scales (fill = cover the box and crop overflow, fit = show the whole image with possible gaps, crop, or tile to repeat), corner rounding, width and height, and tile repeat. Use fit for logos or illustrations you don't want cropped, and fill for photos that should fully cover the box. This appears only for the Image First or Chart First layouts and is hidden for the orbital Circle layout.

guides.name: Screen field: Space around the image
guides.userNeed: Know what "Space around the image" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Space around the image
sections.description: Sets the empty space, in pixels, on each side of the step image: top, right, bottom, left. The default is usually 0; add padding so the image does not touch the title or screen edges and sits balanced in its container. A well-framed visual carries the emotional pull on an ad landing page, so adjust this when the image looks cramped or off-center. This control appears only for the Image First or Chart First layouts.

guides.name: Screen field: Text choices or numbers
guides.userNeed: Know what "Text choices or numbers" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Text choices or numbers
sections.description: Chooses what the picker collects: String for text choices, which allows up to 5 side-by-side wheels (such as month / day / year), or Integer for a single numeric range (such as age or quantity). Set this first — it limits Integer to one wheel, unlocks up to five wheels for String, and changes how each wheel's options are set up below.

guides.name: Screen field: Joiner between wheel values
guides.userNeed: Know what "Joiner between wheel values" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Joiner between wheel values
sections.description: The character or characters used to join selections from multiple wheels into one combined value — for example '/' turns two wheels into 'Large/Red', or a space joins them with a gap. This only matters when you have more than one wheel; leave it as-is for a single-wheel picker. Choose a separator that reads naturally in the answer you'll store and reuse later in the funnel.

guides.name: Screen field: Add and set up wheels
guides.userNeed: Know what "Add and set up wheels" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Add and set up wheels
sections.description: The spinning wheels users scroll to make their choice. Each wheel is either a List of text options or a Range of numbers; use Add Wheel to add more (up to 5 with the String data type, only 1 with Integer), then expand a wheel to set its type, options, and starting value. Each wheel's selection is saved as a variable you can reuse later for personalized copy or to route users down different paths.

guides.name: Screen field: List of options or number range
guides.userNeed: Know what "List of options or number range" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: List of options or number range
sections.description: Sets how this wheel's values are built: List means you type each option yourself (sizes, labels, months), while Range means you set a from/to span and the wheel fills in every number between, such as 1 to 10. Use List for arbitrary text choices and Range for evenly-spaced numbers. Note that switching between them clears the options you've already entered for this wheel.

guides.name: Screen field: Edit the wheel's choices
guides.userNeed: Know what "Edit the wheel's choices" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Edit the wheel's choices
sections.description: The text choices shown on a List-mode wheel. Add, edit, drag to reorder, or delete options (1-20 allowed). The order here is the order users scroll through, so place the most common choices near the top where the starting value lands. Each option is per-language, so translate them if your funnel runs in more than one language.

guides.name: Screen field: Lowest number on the wheel
guides.userNeed: Know what "Lowest number on the wheel" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Lowest number on the wheel
sections.description: The smallest number a Range-mode wheel starts at. Together with the 'to' value it sets the span users can scroll — for example from 1 to 10 lets them pick any number from 1 through 10. Keep this lower than 'to', and set it to the smallest realistic answer for your question, such as a minimum age or quantity.

guides.name: Screen field: Highest number on the wheel
guides.userNeed: Know what "Highest number on the wheel" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Highest number on the wheel
sections.description: The largest number a Range-mode wheel ends at. Together with the 'from' value it sets the span users can scroll — for example from 1 to 10 lets them pick any number from 1 through 10. Keep this higher than 'from', and set it to the largest realistic answer for your question so users aren't offered absurd values.

guides.name: Screen field: Pre-selected starting value
guides.userNeed: Know what "Pre-selected starting value" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Pre-selected starting value
sections.description: The value already showing when the screen loads. For List wheels, pick one of your options; for Range wheels, pick any number within the from/to span. Pre-selecting the most common answer reduces friction and prevents accidental empty or extreme submissions — leave it empty only if you truly want nothing chosen up front.

guides.name: Screen field: Size of the selection label
guides.userNeed: Know what "Size of the selection label" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Size of the selection label
sections.description: Text size of the label that shows the user's current choice above the wheels (0-50, default 18). 16-22 keeps the chosen value clearly readable; very small or 0 effectively hides it. Increase it when you want the selection to stand out as a confirmation of what the user picked.

guides.name: Screen field: Thickness of the label text
guides.userNeed: Know what "Thickness of the label text" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Thickness of the label text
sections.description: How heavy the selection label looks, from 300 (Light) to 900 (Black); default 400 (Regular). Use 600-700 (Semibold/Bold) to make the chosen value read as a clear confirmation, or keep it at 400 if it should sit quietly above the wheels. Match it to the weight of your other body text for a consistent look.

guides.name: Screen field: Color of the selection label
guides.userNeed: Know what "Color of the selection label" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Color of the selection label
sections.description: Color of the label text that shows the user's current choice above the wheels (default black, #000000). Pick a color with strong contrast against the container background so the chosen value stays easy to read, ideally your theme's main text color for consistency. This affects only the label, not the wheel options themselves.

guides.name: Screen field: Where the label sits
guides.userNeed: Know what "Where the label sits" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Where the label sits
sections.description: Horizontal position of the selection label within its container: left, center, or right (default center). Center usually lines up with the centered wheels and is the safe choice; switch to left or right only to align the label with other text or a specific layout. This is purely visual and does not change the value the user selected.

guides.name: Screen field: Background behind the wheels
guides.userNeed: Know what "Background behind the wheels" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Background behind the wheels
sections.description: Fill color behind the spinning wheels (default white, #ffffff). Choose a color that contrasts enough with the screen background so the picker reads as its own distinct card and the wheel values stay legible. A subtle off-white or light tint often separates the picker from the page better than pure white.

guides.name: Screen field: Thickness of the picker outline
guides.userNeed: Know what "Thickness of the picker outline" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Thickness of the picker outline
sections.description: Width in pixels of the outline around the picker container (0-50, default 1). Set it to 0 for no border and rely on the background color alone, or use 1-2px for a clean, defined edge. The border color setting below only takes effect when this is greater than 0.

guides.name: Screen field: Color of the picker outline
guides.userNeed: Know what "Color of the picker outline" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Color of the picker outline
sections.description: Color of the outline around the picker container (default light gray, #E0E0E0). Use a light neutral for a subtle card edge, or your accent color to make the picker stand out on the screen. It only shows when the border thickness above is greater than 0.

guides.name: Screen field: Roundness of the corners
guides.userNeed: Know what "Roundness of the corners" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Roundness of the corners
sections.description: How rounded the four corners of the picker container are, in pixels (0-50, default 12). 0 gives sharp square corners; higher values look softer and more modern. Match it to the corner roundness of your buttons and other cards so the whole funnel feels consistent.

guides.name: Screen field: Space inside the picker
guides.userNeed: Know what "Space inside the picker" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Space inside the picker
sections.description: Sets the empty space, in pixels, inside the picker container on each side: top, right, bottom, left, between the border and the spinning wheels. The default is usually a small value; increase it to give the wheels breathing room, or keep it tight for a compact picker. A clean, uncluttered picker feels effortless to use, which helps visitors commit their answer and continue through the funnel.

guides.name: Screen field: Keep custom code sandboxed
guides.userNeed: Know what "Keep custom code sandboxed" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Keep custom code sandboxed
sections.description: Decides whether your custom HTML runs in a protected sandbox (On, the default) or directly in the page (Off). Leave it On — the sandbox stops your CSS and JavaScript from leaking out and breaking the rest of the screen. Only switch it Off if your code truly needs to reach the surrounding page, and expect to debug styling clashes if you do.

guides.name: Screen field: Your custom screen code
guides.userNeed: Know what "Your custom screen code" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Your custom screen code
sections.description: Write the HTML, CSS, and JavaScript that renders inside this custom screen here. Edits stay local until you click Apply to Preview, then they appear in the preview. Critically, your code must call segmentlySDK.navigateNext to advance the funnel and segmentlySDK.getChildSection to read any data sources you've added — without navigateNext, visitors get stuck and never reach your paywall.

guides.name: Screen field: Editable content for your HTML
guides.userNeed: Know what "Editable content for your HTML" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Editable content for your HTML
sections.description: Adds reusable pieces of content (text, images, and more) that your custom HTML can read by name, so copy and visuals live in the editor instead of being hard-coded. In code you fetch one by its name, which lets you or a non-developer update content later without touching the HTML. The Image URL Scanner can auto-create media sources from external image links it finds, so those images get hosted and tracked by Segmently.

guides.name: Screen field: Show a close (X) button
guides.userNeed: Know what "Show a close (X) button" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Show a close (X) button
sections.description: Adds the X in the header that lets people dismiss the paywall and keep browsing. For paid-ad traffic keep it on (optionally with a short reveal delay) — an inescapable paywall hurts trust and can break app-store and ad-network rules. Turn it off only when you deliberately want a hard gate users can't skip.

guides.name: Screen field: Color the close (X) icon
guides.userNeed: Know what "Color the close (X) icon" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Color the close (X) icon
sections.description: Sets the color of the X dismiss icon (default white; applies only when the close button is shown). Choose a color that contrasts with whatever sits behind the header — dark over a light hero image, white over a dark one — so users can always find and tap it. Low contrast here can leave people feeling trapped on the paywall.

guides.name: Screen field: Place the close button left or right
guides.userNeed: Know what "Place the close button left or right" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Place the close button left or right
sections.description: Puts the X on the start side (left in most languages, right in right-to-left ones) or the end side of the header; the sides flip automatically by language. Default to the start/top-left to match common mobile paywall convention. Move it to the end only when your hero layout needs that corner kept clear.

guides.name: Screen field: When the close button appears
guides.userNeed: Know what "When the close button appears" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: When the close button appears
sections.description: Controls when the X becomes tappable: right away, or after a short timer that lets users take in the offer first (set the length in the delay field below). For ad traffic, showing it immediately or after a 2-3 second delay converts well without feeling like a trap. Avoid long delays that frustrate users or break ad-network rules.

guides.name: Screen field: How long to delay the X
guides.userNeed: Know what "How long to delay the X" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: How long to delay the X
sections.description: How long the close button stays hidden (1-30 seconds) when you've set it to appear after a timer; it has no effect otherwise. A short 2-3 seconds nudges users to read the offer first without feeling trapped. Longer delays raise frustration and drop-off, so reserve 10s or more only for a deliberate hard gate.

guides.name: Screen field: Show a restore-purchases link
guides.userNeed: Know what "Show a restore-purchases link" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Show a restore-purchases link
sections.description: Adds a small 'Restore Purchases' control in the header so returning buyers can recover an existing subscription instead of paying twice. Keep it on: a working restore option is effectively required on app-store paywalls and it reassures buyers, which protects conversions. There's also a Restore link available in the footer legal links, so use whichever placement fits your layout.

guides.name: Screen field: Edit the restore link wording
