guides.userNeed: Know what "Edit the restore link wording" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Edit the restore link wording
sections.description: The text shown on the header restore link, editable for each language you support (default 'Restore Purchases'). Keep it close to the standard 'Restore Purchases' wording so returning buyers instantly recognize it. Add other-language versions only if your funnel actually ships in multiple languages.

guides.name: Screen field: Restore link background fill
guides.userNeed: Know what "Restore link background fill" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Restore link background fill
sections.description: Adds a colored background block behind the restore link text. Most restore links sit on the plain header with no fill, so the default is none — leave it unset for the usual text-only look. Set a color only if you want a chip or pill behind the link, then shape it with the opacity and corner-radius fields below.

guides.name: Screen field: Pick the restore link typeface
guides.userNeed: Know what "Pick the restore link typeface" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Pick the restore link typeface
sections.description: Chooses the font for the restore link (SF Pro, SF Pro Rounded, SF Mono, or New York; default SF Pro). Match it to the font used elsewhere on the paywall so the screen looks consistent and trustworthy. There's rarely a reason to give the restore link its own typeface, so SF Pro is a safe choice.

guides.name: Screen field: Restore link line spacing
guides.userNeed: Know what "Restore link line spacing" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Restore link line spacing
sections.description: Sets the vertical space between lines of the restore text. The link is almost always one short line, so this usually has no visible effect — leave it at the default. Only raise it slightly if your custom restore text wraps to multiple lines and the lines look crowded.

guides.name: Screen field: Size the restore link text
guides.userNeed: Know what "Size the restore link text" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Size the restore link text
sections.description: Sets how large the restore link reads, in points (0-50). Keep it small and secondary — around 12-14pt — so it stays legible but doesn't compete with your headline or purchase button. Restore is a recovery option, not a primary action, so resist sizing it up.

guides.name: Screen field: Set the restore link boldness
guides.userNeed: Know what "Set the restore link boldness" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Set the restore link boldness
sections.description: Controls how heavy the restore link text looks (for example Normal or Semibold). Use a normal weight so restore stays a quiet secondary link and doesn't pull attention from your purchase button. Bump it to semibold only if it's genuinely hard to read against the background.

guides.name: Screen field: Color the restore link text
guides.userNeed: Know what "Color the restore link text" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Color the restore link text
sections.description: Sets the restore link's text color (default a muted gray). Check it against your header background first — that gray default disappears on a dark hero, so use a lighter tint there. Keep it readable but understated so restore reads as a secondary link, with enough contrast to stay accessible.

guides.name: Screen field: Align the restore link text
guides.userNeed: Know what "Align the restore link text" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Align the restore link text
sections.description: Sets where the restore link sits in its row — start (left in most languages), center, or end (right) — flipping automatically for right-to-left languages. Usually align it to the side opposite the close button, or center it, so the header reads cleanly. The default works for most layouts.

guides.name: Screen field: Restore link strikethrough color
guides.userNeed: Know what "Restore link strikethrough color" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Restore link strikethrough color
sections.description: Colors a line struck through the restore text, but only if you have deliberately added a crossed-out segment to that text. A standard 'Restore Purchases' link has no strikethrough, so leave this alone — it does nothing unless your custom text actually contains a struck-through part.

guides.name: Screen field: Restore background transparency
guides.userNeed: Know what "Restore background transparency" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Restore background transparency
sections.description: Controls how see-through the restore link's background fill is, from 0 (invisible) to 1 (solid). It only has an effect once you've set a background color above. Use a partial value for a faint chip behind the text so it stays readable over a busy hero image; otherwise leave it alone.

guides.name: Screen field: Restore background rounding
guides.userNeed: Know what "Restore background rounding" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Restore background rounding
sections.description: Rounds the corners of the restore link's background block, from 0 (sharp rectangle) up to 50 (full pill). It only shows once you've given the link a background color and opacity. Use a higher value for a pill-shaped chip; the default of 0 is fine, and you can ignore it entirely if there's no background fill.

guides.name: Screen field: Show featured media
guides.userNeed: Know what "Show featured media" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Show featured media
sections.description: Turn this on to show a featured image or video at the top of the paywall, or off to hide media and give the plan cards more room. After enabling, choose the media type and upload your asset, otherwise nothing appears. Use media when a visual strengthens the offer; skip it for a tighter, text-only paywall.

guides.name: Screen field: Image or video
guides.userNeed: Know what "Image or video" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Image or video
sections.description: Picks whether the featured media is an image or a video. Image is simplest and loads fastest; video can show your product in motion but should be short and auto-playing. Note that switching type clears any asset you already uploaded, so choose first, then upload; picking Video also unlocks the loop option.

guides.name: Screen field: How the media fills its area
guides.userNeed: Know what "How the media fills its area" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: How the media fills its area
sections.description: Decides how your image or video sits in its space. 'Fit' shows the whole asset but may leave blank bars around it; 'Fill' crops the edges so the area is covered with no gaps. Fill usually looks best for a clean edge-to-edge hero, just keep anything important away from the edges; choose Fit only when the entire image must stay visible.

guides.name: Screen field: Media height on screen
guides.userNeed: Know what "Media height on screen" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Media height on screen
sections.description: How much of the screen the featured image or video takes up, as a share of screen height. Keep it moderate (around 30 to 45%) so the plan cards and purchase button stay visible without scrolling; too tall pushes your offer below the fold and costs you sales. Always check the result on a phone-sized preview.

guides.name: Screen field: Round the media corners
guides.userNeed: Know what "Round the media corners" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Round the media corners
sections.description: Sets how rounded the corners of the image or video are. Zero gives sharp edges, which often look best for a full-width hero, while higher values give a soft, card-like look that matches rounded buttons and plan cards. Match it to the rest of your theme's rounding; the default is usually fine.

guides.name: Screen field: Loop the video
guides.userNeed: Know what "Loop the video" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Loop the video
sections.description: When on, the featured video repeats continuously; when off, it plays once and stops on the last frame. Loop short, ambient clips (a few seconds) so the paywall stays lively and eye-catching; turn it off for a video with a clear ending you don't want replayed. This only appears when the media type is Video.

guides.name: Screen field: Space around the media
guides.userNeed: Know what "Space around the media" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Space around the media
sections.description: Sets the space between the media and its surroundings on each side: top, right, bottom, and left. Add padding to inset the image or video from the screen edges for a framed look, or set it to zero for a full-bleed, edge-to-edge hero. The theme default is a safe start; adjust only if the media looks too tight or too floaty in preview.

guides.name: Screen field: Where media starts vertically
guides.userNeed: Know what "Where media starts vertically" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Where media starts vertically
sections.description: Sets where the image or video begins at the top of the screen relative to the header (back button and progress bar). 'Screen Top' starts media at the very top behind the header for a full-bleed hero look; 'Header Bottom' starts it just under the header so the controls stay clear of the image. Use Header Bottom if the header overlaps your media awkwardly, otherwise Screen Top is the most immersive.

guides.name: Screen field: How media meets the text
guides.userNeed: Know what "How media meets the text" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: How media meets the text
sections.description: Sets how the media and the paywall text relate vertically. 'Above Content' keeps the media as a banner with the title, subtitle, and plans stacked below it (safest, always readable); 'Behind Intro Content' layers the title over the media for a magazine-style hero. Start with Above Content; if you choose the overlaid look, turn on the gradient overlay so the text stays legible.

guides.name: Screen field: Dark fade over media
guides.userNeed: Know what "Dark fade over media" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Dark fade over media
sections.description: Lays a dark fade over the image or video so any text and buttons placed on top stay readable. Turn it on whenever you layer the headline or content over the media, or when a busy or light image makes text hard to read; leave it off for a clean image with nothing on top. Once on, you can fine-tune its height and color below.

guides.name: Screen field: Gradient coverage
guides.userNeed: Know what "Gradient coverage" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Gradient coverage
sections.description: How far up the media the dark fade reaches, as a percentage. A low value shades only the bottom edge (enough for text sitting near the bottom); a high value darkens most of the image. Set it just high enough to cover where your overlaid text sits, leaving the rest of the image visible. This only appears when the gradient overlay is turned on.

guides.name: Screen field: Gradient overlay color
guides.userNeed: Know what "Gradient overlay color" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Gradient overlay color
sections.description: Sets the color of the dark fade laid over your media (default black). Black works best behind white text; choose a dark brand color if you want the fade to feel on-theme. The overlay always fades to clear at the top, so only this base color matters. It appears only when the gradient overlay is turned on.

guides.name: Screen field: Upload the featured image
guides.userNeed: Know what "Upload the featured image" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Upload the featured image
sections.description: Upload (or clear) the hero image shown at the top of the paywall. Use a high-resolution image with its subject centered, since the edges may be cropped depending on your fit setting. If your funnel runs in multiple languages you can upload a different image per language; it appears only when media type is Image, and nothing shows until you upload one.

guides.name: Screen field: Upload the featured video
guides.userNeed: Know what "Upload the featured video" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Upload the featured video
sections.description: Upload (or clear) the hero video shown at the top of the paywall. Keep it short and lightweight (a few seconds, compressed) so it loads fast on mobile data, and remember it auto-plays muted, so the visual must work without sound. If your funnel runs in multiple languages you can upload a different video per language; it appears only when media type is Video, and nothing shows until you upload one.

guides.name: Screen field: Paywall headline
guides.userNeed: Know what "Paywall headline" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Paywall headline
sections.description: The big headline at the top of the paywall, your one shot to state your strongest benefit in a few words (e.g. 'Reach your goal in 4 weeks'). You can insert @variables like @{user.name} to echo answers the user gave earlier, which makes the offer feel personal and lifts conversion. Turn it off to hide the headline entirely.

guides.name: Screen field: Style the paywall headline
guides.userNeed: Know what "Style the paywall headline" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Style the paywall headline
sections.description: Styles the headline: font, size, weight, color, alignment, and the spacing around it. Keep it large and high-contrast so the main benefit is the first thing the eye lands on. Most users can leave the theme defaults; change them only if the title is hard to read against your background.

guides.name: Screen field: Supporting subtitle
guides.userNeed: Know what "Supporting subtitle" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Supporting subtitle
sections.description: The supporting line just under the headline. Use it to back up the promise with a reason to believe or a specific outcome (e.g. 'Cancel anytime, no questions asked'). You can drop in @variables to reference the user's earlier answers for a personal touch. Turn it off to hide the subtitle.

guides.name: Screen field: Style the paywall subtitle
guides.userNeed: Know what "Style the paywall subtitle" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Style the paywall subtitle
sections.description: Styles the subtitle line: font, size, weight, color, alignment, and the spacing around it. Keep it smaller and lighter than the headline so the main benefit stays dominant. Leave the theme defaults unless the subtitle is hard to read against your background.

guides.name: Screen field: Benefit checklist
guides.userNeed: Know what "Benefit checklist" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Benefit checklist
sections.description: The list of benefits below the subtitle, your main proof the offer is worth paying for. Add one bullet per concrete benefit (what's included, guarantees, results), each with a title, optional subtitle, and icon, and drag to reorder. Aim for 3 to 5 punchy bullets, since too many dilute the message. Use 'Add Bullet' to create one, or clone an existing bullet to keep the styling consistent.

guides.name: Screen field: Style the feature bullets
guides.userNeed: Know what "Style the feature bullets" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Style the feature bullets
sections.description: Sets the background color, border, and corner rounding applied to every bullet in the list at once. Use a subtle card background or border only if you want the bullets to read as a grouped card; otherwise the theme defaults look cleanest. Styling once keeps all bullets consistent.

guides.name: Screen field: Space inside each bullet
guides.userNeed: Know what "Space inside each bullet" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Space inside each bullet
sections.description: Sets the breathing room inside each bullet, between its text or icon and the bullet's edge, adjustable on the top, bottom, left, and right. Increase it if bullets feel cramped, decrease it to fit more on screen. The theme default is usually fine, so tweak only if the spacing looks off in preview.

guides.name: Screen field: Space around the bullet list
guides.userNeed: Know what "Space around the bullet list" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Space around the bullet list
sections.description: Sets the space around the whole list of bullets, separating it from the subtitle above and the plans below. (Bullet padding spaces the inside of one bullet; this spaces the entire group.) Add space if the list feels jammed against the title or the plan cards; the theme default is a safe start.

guides.name: Screen field: Style the bullet titles
guides.userNeed: Know what "Style the bullet titles" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Style the bullet titles
sections.description: Styles the main line of every feature bullet: font, size, weight, color, alignment, and spacing, applied to all bullets at once. Keep bullet titles bold and easy to read so each benefit lands at a glance. The theme defaults usually work, so change them only if a benefit is hard to read.

guides.name: Screen field: Style the bullet subtitles
guides.userNeed: Know what "Style the bullet subtitles" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Style the bullet subtitles
sections.description: Styles the secondary line under each bullet title: font, size, weight, color, alignment, and spacing, applied to all bullets at once. Keep it smaller and lighter than the bullet title so the benefit itself stays the focus. Leave the theme defaults unless the text is hard to read.

guides.name: Screen field: Style the bullet icons
guides.userNeed: Know what "Style the bullet icons" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Style the bullet icons
sections.description: Styles the small icon or image on each bullet: how it sits in its box (fit shows the whole image, fill crops it to cover), how rounded the corners are, and the spacing around it, applied to all bullets at once. Keep icon size and shape consistent so the checklist looks tidy. The theme defaults are a safe start.

guides.name: Screen field: Plan card arrangement
guides.userNeed: Know what "Plan card arrangement" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Plan card arrangement
sections.description: Choose how the plan cards are laid out. Vertical stacks them one under another, which reads best on mobile and works well for 2 to 4 plans; Horizontal lines them up side by side as compact cards, good for 2 short price options you want compared at a glance. Start with Vertical unless you specifically need a side-by-side comparison.

guides.name: Screen field: Checkbox placement on plans
guides.userNeed: Know what "Checkbox placement on plans" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Checkbox placement on plans
sections.description: Choose where the selection checkbox sits on each plan card: left, right, or hidden. Left or right makes selecting a plan obvious; Hidden removes the checkbox and lets the highlighted card itself signal the choice for a cleaner look, but only if your selected style is clearly distinct. Left is a safe default. This also works together with the checkbox styling field below.

guides.name: Screen field: Subscription plans
guides.userNeed: Know what "Subscription plans" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Subscription plans
sections.description: The list of plans the user can buy. Each plan must be linked to a real product in your connected Stripe account, or checkout will fail when you publish. Per plan you set its four corner labels (top-left = plan name, bottom-left = description, top-right = price, bottom-right = billing period) and an optional badge. Mark your best-value plan as selected by default, since the pre-selected plan converts most often. Use 'Add Plan' to add rows.

guides.name: Screen field: Unselected plan style
guides.userNeed: Know what "Unselected plan style" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Unselected plan style
sections.description: How a plan card looks before the user taps it: background color, border, and spacing. Keep this neutral and understated so the chosen plan can clearly stand out against it. The contrast between this and the Selected style is what tells users which plan they've picked, so never make the two look the same.

guides.name: Screen field: Selected plan style
guides.userNeed: Know what "Selected plan style" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Selected plan style
sections.description: How a plan card looks once it's the chosen one: background color, border, and spacing. Make it clearly stand out from the unselected cards, for example a brand-colored border or filled background, so the user is never unsure which plan they're about to buy. Crisp selected styling removes hesitation right before checkout.

guides.name: Screen field: Space inside each plan card
guides.userNeed: Know what "Space inside each plan card" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Space inside each plan card
sections.description: Sets the padding inside each plan card, between its labels and the card edge, on the top, bottom, left, and right. Increase it to make cards feel roomier and easier to tap, decrease it to fit more plans on screen. The theme default is usually fine; adjust only if cards look cramped in preview.

guides.name: Screen field: Plan name vs. price width
guides.userNeed: Know what "Plan name vs. price width" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Plan name vs. price width
sections.description: Sets how much of each plan card's width goes to the left labels (plan name and description), leaving the rest for the right labels (price and billing period). Around 60-70% usually gives names enough room while keeping prices aligned on the right. Lower it if prices look cramped, raise it if plan names wrap awkwardly.

guides.name: Screen field: Space around the plan list
guides.userNeed: Know what "Space around the plan list" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Space around the plan list
sections.description: Sets the space around the whole block of plans, between the list and the screen edges and the content above and below it. (Card padding spaces the inside of one plan; this spaces the entire group.) Add space if the plans feel jammed against the body copy or the purchase button; the theme default is a safe start.

guides.name: Screen field: Style the plan name (top-left)
guides.userNeed: Know what "Style the plan name (top-left)" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Style the plan name (top-left)
sections.description: Styles the top-left label on every plan card, which usually holds the plan name like 'Annual': font, size, weight, color, alignment, and spacing, applied to all plans at once. This only controls how it looks; you edit each plan's actual name in the plan list. Make plan names bold and legible so they're easy to compare; theme defaults usually work.

guides.name: Screen field: Style the plan note (bottom-left)
guides.userNeed: Know what "Style the plan note (bottom-left)" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Style the plan note (bottom-left)
sections.description: Styles the bottom-left label on every plan card, usually the short plan description or trial note: font, size, weight, color, alignment, and spacing, applied to all plans at once. This sets only the look; you write the actual text per plan in the plan list. Keep it smaller and lighter than the plan name; theme defaults are a safe start.

guides.name: Screen field: Style the price (top-right)
guides.userNeed: Know what "Style the price (top-right)" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Style the price (top-right)
sections.description: Styles the top-right label on every plan card, usually the price: font, size, weight, color, alignment, and spacing, applied to all plans at once. The price value itself comes from the linked Stripe product, not here. Make the price bold and prominent so it's easy to compare across plans; theme defaults usually work.

guides.name: Screen field: Style the billing period (bottom-right)
guides.userNeed: Know what "Style the billing period (bottom-right)" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Style the billing period (bottom-right)
sections.description: Styles the bottom-right label on every plan card, usually the billing period like 'per month': font, size, weight, color, alignment, and spacing, applied to all plans at once. The text follows the linked product; this only sets the look. Keep it small and quiet under the price; theme defaults are a safe start.

guides.name: Screen field: Plan badge
guides.userNeed: Know what "Plan badge" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Plan badge
sections.description: An optional ribbon on a plan card, like 'Most Popular' or 'Best Value', used to steer attention to the plan you most want sold. The styling (color, border, position, spacing) is shared across all plans, but the badge text is set per plan, so add text only to the one plan you're promoting. A single well-placed badge lifts conversion; badging every plan cancels the effect.

guides.name: Screen field: Style the plan checkbox
guides.userNeed: Know what "Style the plan checkbox" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Style the plan checkbox
sections.description: Sets the colors of the per-plan checkbox: its unselected (empty) color and its selected (checked) color. It only appears when checkbox placement is set to Left or Right, and is hidden when placement is 'No checkbox'. Use a clear, on-brand selected color so the chosen plan is unmistakable; it defaults to your theme accent.

guides.name: Screen field: Configure purchase button text
guides.userNeed: Know what "Configure purchase button text" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Configure purchase button text
sections.description: Sets the visible label on the purchase subscribe button (default: Subscribe Now). The text supports template variables like pricing, duration, and custom countdown labels for dynamic personalization.

guides.name: Screen field: Style the purchase button label
guides.userNeed: Know what "Style the purchase button label" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Style the purchase button label
sections.description: Controls the look of the text inside the purchase button — font, size, weight, color, alignment, and spacing — not the button box itself, which you style under 'Style purchase button box and appearance'. This is your main call-to-action, so make the label large, bold, and high-contrast against the button fill. Weak or hard-to-read button text directly costs you taps and sales.

guides.name: Screen field: Style the purchase button box
guides.userNeed: Know what "Style the purchase button box" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Style the purchase button box
sections.description: Controls the look of the purchase button itself — fill color, border, corner radius, size, full-width toggle, padding, gradient, shadow, animation, and icon (the label text is styled separately). For ad funnels, a full-width button with a high-contrast accent fill and rounded corners is the proven setup. Make this the boldest element on the screen so the path to purchase is unmistakable.

guides.name: Screen field: Recover users who cancel checkout
guides.userNeed: Know what "Recover users who cancel checkout" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Recover users who cancel checkout
sections.description: Lets you send people who start checkout but back out to a cheaper plan or discount offer instead of just closing the dialog. Catching abandoners this way can recover lost revenue, but you must build that follow-up screen first and connect it here. Leave it empty until you have one — then the dialog simply closes and the user stays on the paywall.

guides.name: Screen field: Set space inside the button
guides.userNeed: Know what "Set space inside the button" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Set space inside the button
sections.description: Sets the padding between the button's label and its edges — top, bottom, left, and right (left/right swap automatically for right-to-left languages). Use generous top and bottom padding so the button feels large and tappable. A cramped call-to-action looks less clickable and lowers taps on mobile.

guides.name: Screen field: Configure auto-renew disclosure text
guides.userNeed: Know what "Configure auto-renew disclosure text" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Configure auto-renew disclosure text
sections.description: Sets the text displayed below the purchase button to explain subscription renewal terms (default: Auto-renews monthly. Cancel anytime.). Supports template variables like duration, price, and custom links.

guides.name: Screen field: Auto-renew disclosure styling
guides.userNeed: Know what "Auto-renew disclosure styling" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Auto-renew disclosure styling
sections.description: Sets the font, size, weight, color, and alignment of the auto-renew disclosure text. Keep it small and quiet relative to your main button — but it must stay clearly readable. App Store and ad-network rules require the renewal terms be legible, so avoid tiny sizes or low-contrast colors that effectively hide the disclosure.

guides.name: Screen field: Order the button and renewal note
guides.userNeed: Know what "Order the button and renewal note" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Order the button and renewal note
sections.description: Sets whether the purchase button sits above the auto-renew disclosure or below it. Button-first is the common, conversion-friendly default. Put the disclosure first when you want the renewal terms visible right above the button so users read them before tapping — often the safer choice for compliance.

guides.name: Screen field: Auto-renew text spacing
guides.userNeed: Know what "Auto-renew text spacing" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Auto-renew text spacing
sections.description: Adds padding around the auto-renew disclosure text on each side — top, bottom, left, and right (left/right flip for right-to-left languages). The defaults are fine for most paywalls; this is optional fine-tuning. Add a little top spacing if you want to separate the disclosure from the button above it.

guides.name: Screen field: Configure restore purchases link
guides.userNeed: Know what "Configure restore purchases link" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Configure restore purchases link
sections.description: Sets the text for the restore purchases link (default: Restore Purchases). This link appears in the legal links section below the auto-renew label and allows users to restore prior subscriptions on iOS.

guides.name: Screen field: Restore link styling
guides.userNeed: Know what "Restore link styling" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Restore link styling
sections.description: Sets the font, size, weight, color, and alignment of the footer 'Restore Purchases' link. Style it to match the Terms and Privacy links beside it so the legal row reads as one consistent group — small and muted, but still legible. Don't make it look like your main button.

guides.name: Screen field: Configure terms of use link
guides.userNeed: Know what "Configure terms of use link" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Configure terms of use link
sections.description: Sets the text for the terms of use link (default: Terms of Use). This link appears in the legal links section and navigates to your terms document when tapped.

guides.name: Screen field: Link your Terms of Use page
guides.userNeed: Know what "Link your Terms of Use page" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Link your Terms of Use page
sections.description: The full https:// web address your Terms of Use link opens when tapped. Fill this in for any paid funnel — a live Terms link is effectively required by app stores and ad networks. Leaving it empty disables the link and leaves your paywall non-compliant, so never ship an ad-ready paywall with this blank.

guides.name: Screen field: Terms link styling
guides.userNeed: Know what "Terms link styling" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Terms link styling
sections.description: Sets the font, size, weight, color, and alignment of the Terms of Use link. Keep it consistent with the Restore and Privacy links beside it — small and muted is fine, but it must stay readable. Burying required legal links in unreadable micro-text invites store rejection and ad-network flags.

guides.name: Screen field: Configure privacy policy link
guides.userNeed: Know what "Configure privacy policy link" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Configure privacy policy link
sections.description: Sets the text for the privacy policy link (default: Privacy Policy). This link appears in the legal links section and navigates to your privacy document when tapped.

guides.name: Screen field: Link your Privacy Policy page
guides.userNeed: Know what "Link your Privacy Policy page" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Link your Privacy Policy page
sections.description: The full https:// web address your Privacy Policy link opens when tapped. Fill this in for any paid funnel — a live Privacy Policy is required by app stores and ad platforms once you collect payment or data. Leaving it empty disables the link and leaves the paywall non-compliant, so don't publish an ad-ready paywall with this blank.

guides.name: Screen field: Privacy link styling
guides.userNeed: Know what "Privacy link styling" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Privacy link styling
sections.description: Sets the font, size, weight, color, and alignment of the Privacy Policy link. Match it to the Restore and Terms links so the legal row looks unified. Small and muted is fine, but it must stay readable — required legal links hidden in unreadable text can get your paywall rejected.

guides.name: Screen field: Color the footer background
guides.userNeed: Know what "Color the footer background" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Color the footer background
sections.description: Sets the fill color of the whole footer block, which holds the purchase button, the auto-renew note, and the legal links (default a dark tone). Pick a color that makes your button pop and keeps the renewal note and legal links readable. If you switch to a light footer, darken those text colors so everything stays legible.

guides.name: Screen field: Legal links row spacing
guides.userNeed: Know what "Legal links row spacing" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Legal links row spacing
sections.description: Adds padding around the whole row of legal links — Restore, Terms, and Privacy together — on each side: top, bottom, left, and right (left/right flip for right-to-left languages). The defaults are fine; this is optional fine-tuning. Add a little top and bottom spacing so the links sit clearly below the disclosure without crowding.

guides.name: Screen field: Add a new section
guides.userNeed: Know what "Add a new section" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Add a new section
sections.description: Use + Add to choose what kind of block to place on this FlexibleLayout screen: text, media, product catalog, button, purchase button, list, custom embed, text field, spacer, header, footer, or paywall header. Add sections in the same order a visitor should read them, then drag to reorder if the screen flow changes. Start with the biggest structure first — for example header, hero text/media, products, and CTA — then tune layout settings inside each section.

guides.name: Screen field: Open screen-level layout settings
guides.userNeed: Know what "Open screen-level layout settings" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Open screen-level layout settings
sections.description: The gear beside the Sections title opens settings for the whole FlexibleLayout screen, not for one individual section. Use it to control whether the full screen scrolls and how much padding the whole stack has from the screen edges. Open this before editing individual section padding when the entire screen feels too close to the phone edge or when you need a fixed, non-scrolling composition.

guides.name: Screen field: Let the whole screen scroll
guides.userNeed: Know what "Let the whole screen scroll" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Let the whole screen scroll
sections.description: When Scrollable screen is on, sections stack vertically and the visitor can scroll through them. Use this for long paywalls, product catalogs, benefit lists, or any screen with more content than fits on a phone. When it is off, the screen uses flexGrow and flexShrink to distribute sections inside one viewport, which is better for fixed hero layouts where the CTA should stay visible without scrolling.

guides.name: Screen field: Space around the whole section stack
guides.userNeed: Know what "Space around the whole section stack" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Space around the whole section stack
sections.description: Container padding adds space between the phone edges and all sections on the screen. It is different from Section padding: container padding moves the entire stack inward, while section padding adds space inside one selected section. Use container padding first when every block feels too close to the screen edge, then use per-section padding only where a specific block needs more breathing room.

guides.name: Screen field: Reorder sections
guides.userNeed: Know what "Reorder sections" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Reorder sections
sections.description: Drag the handle beside a section name to change the vertical reading order on the screen. The order here is the order visitors see in the preview and published flow, so keep the persuasion sequence clear: context first, offer/details next, then the CTA. After reordering, recheck fixed-height and flex settings because a section that worked in one position may need different spacing in another.

guides.name: Screen field: Rename a section for editing
guides.userNeed: Know what "Rename a section for editing" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Rename a section for editing
sections.description: Click the pencil beside a section name to give it a clear internal label, such as Hero headline, Annual plan list, or Bottom CTA. This name helps editors understand the structure and is not shown to visitors. Rename repeated sections immediately so it is obvious which block you are opening, especially when several Text or Button sections exist on the same screen.

guides.name: Screen field: Delete a section
guides.userNeed: Know what "Delete a section" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Delete a section
sections.description: Use the trash icon to remove a section from the screen. Deleting also removes that section's content and can affect buttons linked to it, so confirm only after checking the preview and any parent-section links. If you are unsure, rename the section first or move it lower in the order while you verify the layout instead of deleting it immediately.

guides.name: Screen field: Open one section's settings
guides.userNeed: Know what "Open one section's settings" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Open one section's settings
sections.description: Click the gear inside a section card to open that section's own settings. The first panel controls the section container — height, flex, scrollability, background, borders, alignment, padding, and margin — and the panel below controls the section's content, such as text, media, products, or button styling. This is the main place to tune how one block looks and behaves.

guides.name: Screen field: How tall this section is
guides.userNeed: Know what "How tall this section is" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: How tall this section is
sections.description: Decides how the section's height is calculated. Auto (the safe default) makes it exactly as tall as its content, which is right for most text and buttons. Fixed lets you type an exact pixel height, and Percent sets it to a share of the screen, handy for a hero image that should always fill, say, the top 40 percent. Your pick also decides which value box below applies.

guides.name: Screen field: The height number
guides.userNeed: Know what "The height number" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: The height number
sections.description: This is the number that pairs with your height mode. With Fixed mode, type pixels (0 to 1000, for example 320 for a tall hero); with Percent mode, type a share of the screen (0 to 100, for example 40). The box is ignored in Auto mode. For a scrollable section, this also sets the visible window the content scrolls inside.

guides.name: Screen field: Stretch to fill empty space
guides.userNeed: Know what "Stretch to fill empty space" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Stretch to fill empty space
sections.description: Controls how much leftover vertical space a section soaks up so the screen has no awkward gap. 0 keeps a section at its natural size (the default for text and buttons); 1 or more lets it stretch, and a section set to 2 takes twice the extra space as one set to 1. Raise this on your image or hero section to push the button down to a comfortable spot. Only applies when the section isn't set to scroll.

guides.name: Screen field: Let it shrink on small screens
guides.userNeed: Know what "Let it shrink on small screens" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Let it shrink on small screens
sections.description: Controls which section gives up height first when everything can't fit on a small phone. Higher numbers shrink sooner; 0 means never shrink this one. The default of 1 lets sections shrink evenly. Set 0 on must-stay pieces like the button or logo, and raise it on a less important section like a tall image, so the key content survives intact on the smallest screens.

guides.name: Screen field: Let this section scroll on its own
guides.userNeed: Know what "Let this section scroll on its own" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Let this section scroll on its own
sections.description: Turn on to let a section scroll independently when its content is taller than the height you set (works only with a Fixed or Percent height, not Auto). Use it for a long list of terms or bullets you want capped inside a fixed window while the rest of the screen stays put. Leave off (the default) for normal sections that just sit in the layout.

guides.name: Screen field: Which section sits in front
guides.userNeed: Know what "Which section sits in front" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Which section sits in front
sections.description: When two sections overlap, this decides which one shows on top. A higher number wins; the default 0 is fine as long as nothing overlaps. You only need it when you've deliberately layered sections, like a headline placed over a background image, so give the part you want visible the higher number.

guides.name: Screen field: Solid color or image behind
guides.userNeed: Know what "Solid color or image behind" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Solid color or image behind
sections.description: Sets what fills the area behind this section's content. Solid (the default) uses one color you pick below; Media places an image behind the content for a richer, ad-style look. If you go with Media and put text on top, keep the text readable with a darker image or an overlay so your value proposition doesn't get lost.

guides.name: Screen field: Background fill color
guides.userNeed: Know what "Background fill color" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Background fill color
sections.description: Sets the color behind this section's content, used when the background type is Solid. The default is white. Enter a hex code or pick a swatch, and keep it in line with your theme so the screen feels on-brand, with enough contrast against the text on top to stay readable.

guides.name: Screen field: Round the section corners
guides.userNeed: Know what "Round the section corners" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Round the section corners
sections.description: Rounds all four corners of the section. The default 0 keeps them sharp and square; higher values (try 8 to 16) give a soft card look that pairs well with a solid background or border to make the section stand out as its own block. The range is 0 to 50 pixels.

guides.name: Screen field: Outline thickness
guides.userNeed: Know what "Outline thickness" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Outline thickness
sections.description: Draws an outline around the section. The default 0 means no border; 1 to 2 pixels gives a subtle frame that makes a section read as a self-contained card or highlights an offer. Set this above 0 first, then pick the border color below.

guides.name: Screen field: Outline color
guides.userNeed: Know what "Outline color" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Outline color
sections.description: Sets the color of the section's outline. The default is black, and it only shows when the border thickness is above 0, so set a width first. Match it to one of your theme's accent colors for a clean, on-brand frame around the section.

guides.name: Screen field: Top, center, or bottom
guides.userNeed: Know what "Top, center, or bottom" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Top, center, or bottom
sections.description: Pins the content to the Top, Center, or Bottom of the section. It only changes anything when the section is taller than its content, for example with a Fixed or Percent height or a section stretched to fill space. Use Center to vertically center a headline in a tall hero, or Bottom to push a caption to the base of an image.

guides.name: Screen field: Left, center, or right
guides.userNeed: Know what "Left, center, or right" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Left, center, or right
sections.description: Positions the content along the section's width: Left, Center, or Right. Center is the usual choice for headlines and buttons, while Left reads more naturally for longer body copy. (Left and right follow text direction, so they flip on right-to-left languages.)

guides.name: Screen field: Breathing room inside the section
guides.userNeed: Know what "Breathing room inside the section" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Breathing room inside the section
sections.description: Padding is the space inside a section, between its edges and the content sitting in it. Set Top, Bottom, Left, and Right independently, starting from 0. Add some so text and buttons don't crowd the section border or a background image; 16-24 px all around is a comfortable, readable starting point.

guides.name: Screen field: Space between sections
guides.userNeed: Know what "Space between sections" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Space between sections
sections.description: Margin is the gap outside a section, between it and the sections next to it. Set Top, Bottom, Left, and Right independently, using positive values to push sections apart. A negative top margin pulls a section up so it overlaps the one above — for example, a headline resting on a hero image; pair that with stacking order to control what sits in front.

guides.name: Screen field: The words in this section
guides.userNeed: Know what "The words in this section" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: The words in this section
sections.description: Sets the headline or body text shown here. You can drop in dynamic values by typing @ to pick a flow variable, so the screen can echo the visitor's earlier answer, show a label, or run a live countdown, which makes the funnel feel personal and converts better. If your funnel runs in more than one language, this text can be translated per language.

guides.name: Screen field: Text size
guides.userNeed: Know what "Text size" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Text size
sections.description: Sets the font size in points, where bigger means more prominent. As a guide, about 24 to 40 works for a headline and 14 to 18 for body copy, keeping a clear hierarchy. This overrides your theme's default size for this text, so change it only when this section needs to stand apart from the rest.

guides.name: Screen field: Pick the font
guides.userNeed: Know what "Pick the font" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Pick the font
sections.description: Sets which typeface this text uses. By default it follows your theme font, which keeps the whole funnel looking consistent, so change it only for a deliberate accent. Stick to one or two fonts across the funnel so it reads as polished and on-brand to paid visitors.

guides.name: Screen field: How heavy the text looks
guides.userNeed: Know what "How heavy the text looks" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: How heavy the text looks
sections.description: Controls how thick the text appears. Common picks are 400 for regular body copy, 600 for semibold, and 700 for bold headlines and call-to-action lines. Put the heaviest weight on the one line you most want visitors to notice and keep body text lighter, so the screen has an easy-to-read hierarchy.

guides.name: Screen field: Text color
guides.userNeed: Know what "Text color" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Text color
sections.description: Sets the color of this text. The default is black. Always check it against the section background: dark text on light backgrounds, and light or white text over dark or image backgrounds. Low-contrast text is hard to read and a common reason visitors bounce, so keep your message legible.

guides.name: Screen field: Spacing between lines
guides.userNeed: Know what "Spacing between lines" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Spacing between lines
sections.description: Controls the vertical gap between lines in a multi-line block. Roughly 1.3 to 1.5 times the font size reads comfortably for body copy, with tighter spacing for big headlines. Bump it up if a paragraph feels cramped, or down if a headline's lines drift apart. It only matters when text wraps to more than one line.

guides.name: Screen field: Left, center, or right text
guides.userNeed: Know what "Left, center, or right text" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Left, center, or right text
sections.description: Sets whether the text reads from the Left, Center, or Right. Center suits short headlines and call-to-action lines, while Left is easier to read for longer body copy. (Left and right follow language direction and flip on right-to-left locales.)

guides.name: Screen field: How the image fills its area
guides.userNeed: Know what "How the image fills its area" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: How the image fills its area
sections.description: Decides how your image or video fits the section. Fill covers the whole area and crops the edges that don't fit — best for full-bleed hero shots and the right pick for most ad creatives. Fit shows the entire image but may leave blank bars around it; use it when nothing can be cropped. Stretch forces an exact fit but distorts the picture, so avoid it for photos.

guides.name: Screen field: How much height the image takes
guides.userNeed: Know what "How much height the image takes" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: How much height the image takes
sections.description: Sets how much of the section's height the image or video fills, as a percentage. The default 50 splits the space evenly and leaves the lower half for your headline and button. Raise it (around 70) for a bold, image-led screen, or lower it when you need more room for copy and a clear call to action.

guides.name: Screen field: Round the image corners
guides.userNeed: Know what "Round the image corners" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Round the image corners
sections.description: Rounds the corners of the image or video. The default 0 is square; try 8 to 16 for a soft, modern look or a higher value for a strongly rounded card. Match it to the rounding on nearby buttons and sections so the whole screen feels cohesive.

guides.name: Screen field: Where the image starts on screen
guides.userNeed: Know what "Where the image starts on screen" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Where the image starts on screen
sections.description: Sets the top edge of your image or video. Screen Top runs it all the way up behind the status bar and header for a full-bleed, edge-to-edge hero. Header Bottom starts it just below the header bar so a back button or progress bar stays clearly visible. Pick Screen Top for an immersive opener, Header Bottom when the header needs to read cleanly.

guides.name: Screen field: Text below or over the image
guides.userNeed: Know what "Text below or over the image" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Text below or over the image
sections.description: Decides whether your text and buttons sit below the image or float on top of it. Below media keeps content in its own space under the image — the safest choice for readability. Overlapping media lets the headline drift over the lower part of the image for a magazine-style hero; if you use it, add an overlay or gradient so the text stays legible against the picture.

guides.name: Screen field: Loop the video
guides.userNeed: Know what "Loop the video" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Loop the video
sections.description: For video media only: turn on to loop the clip continuously, or leave off to play it once and stop. Looping suits short, ambient hero or background videos that keep the screen feeling alive, while play-once suits a clip with a clear start and finish. It has no effect on still images.

guides.name: Screen field: Dark fade for readable text
guides.userNeed: Know what "Dark fade for readable text" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Dark fade for readable text
sections.description: Adds a dark fade over the bottom of the image or video so text placed on top stays readable. It's strongest at the bottom and clears toward the top. The default is black, which is the usual choice (or a dark brand color). Use it whenever you let content overlap the media so your headline and button don't get lost in a busy image.

guides.name: Screen field: Wording on the button
guides.userNeed: Know what "Wording on the button" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Wording on the button
sections.description: The text shown on the button (placeholder 'Button Text'). Use a short, action-led phrase like 'Continue', 'Get Started', or 'Next' so people know exactly what tapping does. If your funnel runs in more than one language, this wording is saved per language, so set it for each one you support.

guides.name: Screen field: Size of the button label
guides.userNeed: Know what "Size of the button label" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Size of the button label
sections.description: Sets how large the text on the button appears. Most buttons read well at 16-18; go larger to make a primary action more prominent, but watch that the label doesn't wrap or overflow on small phone screens. Keep it consistent across your buttons so the screen looks intentional.

guides.name: Screen field: Font for the button text
guides.userNeed: Know what "Font for the button text" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Font for the button text
sections.description: Picks the typeface used for the button label. Leave it on your theme default so the button matches the rest of your funnel — mixing fonts on one screen looks unpolished and can hurt trust. Only override it when your brand requires a specific font.

guides.name: Screen field: Boldness of the label
guides.userNeed: Know what "Boldness of the label" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Boldness of the label
sections.description: Sets how thick the button text is, from 400 (regular) through 700 (bold) and beyond. Bolder text draws the eye, so use 600-700 for a primary action you want people to tap. Keep lighter weights for secondary or less important buttons.

guides.name: Screen field: Set button text color
guides.userNeed: Know what "Set button text color" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Set button text color
sections.description: Hex color for button label text. Default black (#000000). Must contrast with button background for readability.

guides.name: Screen field: Spacing between wrapped lines
guides.userNeed: Know what "Spacing between wrapped lines" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Spacing between wrapped lines
sections.description: Sets the vertical gap between lines when a button label is long enough to wrap onto two or more lines. Most buttons use a single short label, so the default is fine and you can ignore this. Nudge it up only if a multi-line button looks cramped or hard to read.

guides.name: Screen field: Align button text
guides.userNeed: Know what "Align button text" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Align button text
sections.description: Text alignment within button: start (left in LTR), center, or end (right in LTR). Center alignment is typical for buttons.

guides.name: Screen field: Set button color
guides.userNeed: Know what "Set button color" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Set button color
sections.description: Hex color for button background. Default yellow-gold (#ffc201). Primary visual element for call-to-action buttons.

guides.name: Screen field: Round button corners
guides.userNeed: Know what "Round button corners" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Round button corners
sections.description: Uniform corner radius (0-50 pixels) for all button corners. Default 12 creates slightly rounded button. Higher values create pill-shaped buttons.

guides.name: Screen field: Set button border thickness
guides.userNeed: Know what "Set button border thickness" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Set button border thickness
sections.description: Button border stroke width in pixels (0-50). Default 0 (no border). Used with border color for outlined button style.

guides.name: Screen field: Set button border color
guides.userNeed: Know what "Set button border color" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Set button border color
sections.description: Hex color for button border line. Only visible when border width is greater than 0.

guides.name: Screen field: Gradient color fill
guides.userNeed: Know what "Gradient color fill" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Gradient color fill
sections.description: Optional. Layers a color gradient over the button's solid background for a richer, more premium look. Pick Simple (two colors), Medium (two colors plus a tilt angle), or Advanced (several color stops, with optional shimmer). Leave it off if a flat color is enough; turn it on to make a primary button catch the eye.

guides.name: Screen field: Drop shadow under the button
guides.userNeed: Know what "Drop shadow under the button" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Drop shadow under the button
sections.description: Optional. Casts a soft shadow beneath the button so it appears lifted off the screen, which helps a primary action stand out. Adjust blur for softness, spread for size, opacity for strength, and offset for direction. A subtle shadow usually looks best; leave it off for a flat, minimal style.

guides.name: Screen field: Button visual effects
guides.userNeed: Know what "Button visual effects" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Button visual effects
sections.description: Optional finishing touches for the button, such as overall transparency and entrance or tap animations. Use a subtle animation to draw the eye to a primary call-to-action, or lower the transparency to play down a secondary button. Leave it off for a plain, static button.

guides.name: Screen field: Optional icon on the button
guides.userNeed: Know what "Optional icon on the button" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Optional icon on the button
sections.description: Adds a small image beside the button label, positioned left or right of the text, with controls for its size and surrounding spacing. Use a simple icon to reinforce the action — like an arrow on a 'Continue' button — and upload a transparent PNG or SVG so it sits cleanly. Leave it empty for a clean text-only button.

guides.name: Screen field: Inner spacing around the label
guides.userNeed: Know what "Inner spacing around the label" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Inner spacing around the label
sections.description: Sets the breathing room between the label or icon and the button's edges, set separately for top, bottom, left, and right. More padding makes the button bigger and easier to tap; too little makes it look cramped. Generous top and bottom padding gives a primary button a comfortable, finger-friendly tap area.

guides.name: Screen field: Wording on the buy button
guides.userNeed: Know what "Wording on the buy button" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Wording on the buy button
sections.description: The text on your paywall's purchase button (default 'Subscribe Now'). This is the most important call to action in the whole funnel, so make it clear and benefit-led, such as 'Start My Free Trial' or 'Unlock Full Access'. If you run multiple languages, this wording is saved per language, so translate it for each.

guides.name: Screen field: Purchase button text size
guides.userNeed: Know what "Purchase button text size" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Purchase button text size
sections.description: Sets how big the label on your purchase button looks, measured in points. Since this is your main paywall call-to-action, keep it large and unmistakable — around 17 to 20 pt works well on most screens. Avoid going so big that the text wraps or spills outside the button on smaller phones.

guides.name: Screen field: Purchase button font
guides.userNeed: Know what "Purchase button font" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Purchase button font
sections.description: Picks the typeface for the purchase button label, such as SF Pro or Helvetica. Match it to the rest of your paywall so the call-to-action looks intentional rather than out of place. Leave it on the theme default unless your brand uses a specific font.

guides.name: Screen field: Purchase button text weight
guides.userNeed: Know what "Purchase button text weight" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Purchase button text weight
sections.description: Controls how thick or bold the button label appears, on a scale from 400 (regular) to 700 (bold) and heavier. As your primary call-to-action it should look bold and confident — a weight of 600 to 700 helps it visually dominate any secondary buttons on the screen.

guides.name: Screen field: Purchase button text color
guides.userNeed: Know what "Purchase button text color" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Purchase button text color
sections.description: Sets the color of the words on your purchase button. Make sure it contrasts strongly with the button background so the label stays easy to read — for example, dark text on the default yellow-gold button. Weak contrast means users miss the action, which directly costs you conversions.

guides.name: Screen field: Purchase button line spacing
guides.userNeed: Know what "Purchase button line spacing" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Purchase button line spacing
sections.description: Controls the vertical gap between lines when the button label runs onto two or more lines. Most call-to-action labels fit on one line, so you can leave this on the default. Adjust it only if a longer label looks cramped or too loose when it wraps.

guides.name: Screen field: Purchase button text alignment
guides.userNeed: Know what "Purchase button text alignment" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Purchase button text alignment
sections.description: Sets where the label sits inside the button: start (left in left-to-right languages), center, or end (right). Center is the standard choice and is recommended for a call-to-action so the label reads as one clear, balanced action.

guides.name: Screen field: Set purchase button color
guides.userNeed: Know what "Set purchase button color" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Set purchase button color
sections.description: Hex color for purchase button background. Default yellow-gold (#ffc201). Distinguishes purchase action from regular navigation.

guides.name: Screen field: Roundness of the button corners
guides.userNeed: Know what "Roundness of the button corners" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Roundness of the button corners
sections.description: Rounds all four corners of the purchase button by the same amount, from sharp to fully rounded (0-50). The default of about 12 gives a softly rounded look; raise it toward 50 for a pill-shaped button, or set 0 for crisp square corners. Match it to your other buttons so the paywall feels cohesive.

guides.name: Screen field: Purchase button border thickness
guides.userNeed: Know what "Purchase button border thickness" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Purchase button border thickness
sections.description: Sets how thick the outline around the purchase button is, from 0 to 50 pixels. The default is 0, meaning no border; set a value together with a border color to create an outlined button. A solid filled button usually converts better, so most paywalls leave this at 0.

guides.name: Screen field: Purchase button border color
guides.userNeed: Know what "Purchase button border color" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Purchase button border color
sections.description: Sets the color of the outline around the purchase button. It only shows up when the border thickness is above 0, so set a thickness first. Use it to give an outlined-style call-to-action a clean, contrasting edge.

guides.name: Screen field: Purchase button gradient
guides.userNeed: Know what "Purchase button gradient" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Purchase button gradient
sections.description: Optionally lays a color gradient over the button's solid background for a richer call-to-action. Pick Simple (two colors), Medium (two colors plus an angle), or Advanced (multiple color stops, with an optional shimmer). Use it to make your main CTA pop; leave it off if a flat color already stands out.

guides.name: Screen field: Purchase button shadow
guides.userNeed: Know what "Purchase button shadow" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Purchase button shadow
sections.description: Optionally adds a soft shadow beneath the button so it lifts off the screen and pulls the eye toward your call-to-action. You can tune the softness (blur), size (spread), strength (opacity), and direction (offset). A subtle shadow usually works best; leave it off for a flat design.

guides.name: Screen field: Purchase button effects
guides.userNeed: Know what "Purchase button effects" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Purchase button effects
sections.description: Optional finishing touches for the purchase button, such as overall transparency and entrance or tap animations. A subtle pulse or scale animation can pull attention to your call-to-action and lift conversions. Leave it off for a static button.

guides.name: Screen field: Purchase button icon
guides.userNeed: Know what "Purchase button icon" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Purchase button icon
sections.description: Optionally shows a small image next to the button label, to the left or right of the text. Upload an icon, then set its size and the spacing around it. A lock or arrow icon can reinforce the action, but a clean text-only button works just as well.

guides.name: Screen field: Offer a cheaper plan on cancel
guides.userNeed: Know what "Offer a cheaper plan on cancel" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Offer a cheaper plan on cancel
sections.description: Controls what happens when someone cancels the payment. When on, they're sent to a downsale screen offering a cheaper or alternative plan — a second chance to recover the sale. When off, cancelling just sends them back with no further offer. Only turn this on if you've actually built a downsale screen in the funnel, otherwise there's nothing for it to open.

guides.name: Screen field: Inner spacing around the label
guides.userNeed: Know what "Inner spacing around the label" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Inner spacing around the label
sections.description: Sets the breathing room between the label or icon and the purchase button's edges, set separately for top, bottom, left, and right. More padding makes the button taller and easier to tap; too little looks cramped. Generous top and bottom padding helps your main purchase button feel substantial and inviting to press.

guides.name: Screen field: Pin the CTA to the bottom
guides.userNeed: Know what "Pin the CTA to the bottom" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Pin the CTA to the bottom
sections.description: Turns the sticky bar on or off. When on, your main button stays pinned to the bottom and tappable while the visitor scrolls, and the rest of the bar's settings below appear. Turn it on for long or paywall screens so the action never scrolls out of reach (this protects clicks from paid traffic); leave it off on short screens where the button is always in view.

guides.name: Screen field: Show a bar behind the button
guides.userNeed: Know what "Show a bar behind the button" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Show a bar behind the button
sections.description: Adds a solid bar behind the pinned button and unlocks the background color, opacity, border and corner-radius settings. Keep it on in most cases: the bar separates the CTA from content scrolling underneath, so the button stays readable over busy backgrounds. Turn it off only for a clean floating-button look on simple screens where nothing scrolls behind it.

guides.name: Screen field: Color of the bar
guides.userNeed: Know what "Color of the bar" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Color of the bar
sections.description: Sets the color of the bar behind the pinned button (appears only when the bar is shown; defaults to white). Match it to your screen or theme background so the bar feels built-in, and make sure it contrasts with the button so the CTA stays the most eye-catching thing on screen. That contrast is what keeps the call-to-action obvious to paid-traffic visitors.

guides.name: Screen field: How see-through the bar is
guides.userNeed: Know what "How see-through the bar is" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: How see-through the bar is
sections.description: Sets how transparent the bar's background is, from fully see-through to fully solid (only applies when the bar is shown). Keep it near solid to keep the CTA crisp and readable; lower it for a softer, glass-like look that lets content show through. Avoid going very transparent — if the button blends into scrolling content, visitors may miss it and you lose clicks.

guides.name: Screen field: Roundness of the bar corners
guides.userNeed: Know what "Roundness of the bar corners" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Roundness of the bar corners
sections.description: Sets how rounded the bar's corners are, in pixels (default 12, only applies when the bar is shown). The default looks good on most screens; raise it for a softer, pill-like bar or set it to 0 for sharp corners. Match it to your buttons and cards so the bar looks like part of the design rather than an add-on.

guides.name: Screen field: Outline thickness
guides.userNeed: Know what "Outline thickness" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Outline thickness
sections.description: Sets how thick the outline around the bar is, in pixels (default 0, meaning no outline; only applies when the bar is shown). Add an outline when the bar's color is close to the screen background and you want a crisp edge that separates the CTA from content behind it. Once it is above 0, the border color setting appears so you can style the outline.

guides.name: Screen field: Outline color
guides.userNeed: Know what "Outline color" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Outline color
sections.description: Sets the color of the bar's outline (defaults to black; appears only when the outline thickness is above 0 and the bar is shown). Pick a color that frames the bar without competing with the button — a subtle, theme-matched tone usually works best, keeping attention on the CTA itself.

guides.name: Screen field: Spacing from screen edges
guides.userNeed: Know what "Spacing from screen edges" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Spacing from screen edges
sections.description: Sets the gap, in pixels, between the bar and the top, right, bottom and left edges of the screen. Add a little bottom and side spacing so the bar floats just above the edge instead of touching it. This keeps the CTA clear of the phone's home indicator and gesture area, so the button stays comfortably tappable on mobile, where most paid traffic lands.

guides.name: Screen field: Space around the button
guides.userNeed: Know what "Space around the button" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Space around the button
sections.description: Sets the inner spacing on all four sides between the bar's background and the button inside it. A little padding keeps the button from looking cramped against the edges and gives a comfortable tap target; too much wastes vertical space and shrinks the visible content. Adjust until the button sits centered with even breathing room.

guides.name: Screen field: What the button does
guides.userNeed: Know what "What the button does" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: What the button does
sections.description: Chooses the pinned button's job: a standard button navigates to the next screen (use it on flow steps like 'Continue'), while a purchase button starts checkout and ties into your paywall products (use it on the paywall). The bar holds one button at a time, so switching type replaces it with a fresh default — your bar styling is kept, but you'll need to re-set the button's label and action.

guides.name: Screen field: Pinned button label & style
guides.userNeed: Know what "Pinned button label & style" controls and when to adjust it while editing a screen.

sections.title: Pinned button label & style
sections.description: Opens an inline card to set everything about the pinned button: its label, where it goes (next screen, or for a purchase button, which product it buys), icon, colors, fonts and shadows. The two things that move conversion most are setting the action correctly so the CTA actually leads somewhere, and writing a short benefit-driven label like 'Start free trial'. Style it to stand out clearly against the bar so it stays the obvious next step.
